The Codex pitch is credible: contributors add personas from AGENTS.md, and Codex-run PR review checks realism and weights. Against today's app it turns a generic SaaS template into a memorable product that reps may actually return to.
reviews.no_case: Calm can read as soft, and the proposal's own risk list cites public reviews calling AI roleplay too agreeable. A six-second breathing rhythm and a mandatory 60-second warm-up before every call add friction for a rep with three minutes before a dial. Numbers are off by default, so live scoring against the rubric is shown as trend arrows only, a weaker answer than the brief asks for. The warm editorial palette moves away from the modern, cutting-edge look the brief wants, and the Tailwind 3-to-4 migration touches every screen. The Base UI claim rests on a vendor blog that the proposal itself asks us to verify. The mood-first design is clear, but it puts the 'cutting-edge AI coaching' signal behind a breathing animation.

reviews.yes_case: Fluent Live Coach is a Microsoft Fluent 2 system (Fluent v9 components and Griffel tokens) with a custom deep-teal brand ramp and a violet coach accent kept separate from score colours. It is the most conservative direction, which makes it easy for an enterprise sales org to adopt: a top bar with Practice, Library, Progress and Team, a 264px filter rail, persona cards with avatars and difficulty dots, and a DataGrid list view. The live call uses a dark call stage: a persona avatar with speaking ring, a transcript with beat tags such as 'Pricing: not yet', and a right coach rail with live rubric bars, talk-track progress, one violet whisper at a time, and an amber objection alert with a suggested reply. The debrief is evidence-first: a score ring with a grader provenance chip ('Graded by gpt-4.1-mini, 14 quotes', or an amber keyword-fallback notice), a timeline with jump-to-transcript markers, and accordions per criterion with timestamped quotes. The launch set explicitly covers every job the brief names, and the wizard's 'why' chips link each generated trait to its source sentence. Compared with today's app it adds the coach, the team view and a credible grading story in a structure teams already know.
reviews.no_case: Fluent is a Microsoft design system, and the proposal's own risk section says it can read as Teams or Microsoft. A README line of non-affiliation will not change the look; a judge will see a Teams-style skin with a teal swap. Segoe UI Variable is Windows-only, so the Inter fallback has to be proven on macOS, Linux and Android. The brand ramp, token values and React 19 peer range are unverified, which is a credibility problem before launch. The proposal scores its own distinctiveness at 5.5 and modern at 6.5, and I agree: this is the least cutting-edge direction in the set, and it does not say AI voice coaching in the way the brief asks.

reviews.yes_case: Fluent Live Coach replaces the whole app with one Microsoft Fluent 2 component system (v9 only) on a custom deep-teal brand ramp (seed #0F766E), styled through Griffel tokens and Fluent icons, so every screen shares one set of buttons, cards, tables, drawers, toasts and menus. The live call moves to a dark call stage with a coach rail beside the transcript: rubric bars ease over 300ms when a score changes, one violet whisper cue fades in at a time, and an amber alert appears on objections with a suggested reply. The debrief is an evidence-first scorecard: a score ring with grade, a score-over-time timeline whose markers jump to exact transcript lines, criteria accordions with timestamped quotes, and a provenance chip that names the grader model and quote count, with a visible notice when the keyword fallback grader was used. The persona wizard runs four steps where each generated field carries a 'why' chip linking to the source sentence, then a test drive and a persona-file export for a pull request. Compared with today's light generic skin, a chat-style call screen and no reactions until the call ends, this gives a serious, accessible, enterprise-familiar product that a sales-org buyer reads at a glance, and it keeps OpenAI Realtime, grader and coach models visible in a model-role strip.
reviews.no_case: Fluent is Microsoft's design language, and an MIT project that wants an independent identity risks looking like a Teams skin. A custom teal ramp fixes colour but not the shape of the screens, which will still read as an intranet. It has the weakest distinctiveness of the top group, and its own self-score of 6.5 on look is the honest read. Several facts are unverified before shipping: the Fluent token values, the React 19 peer range, and Segoe UI being Windows-only with an Inter fallback that still needs checking on macOS, Linux and Android. The live coaching promise rests on a coach call of about 2 seconds that has no evidence yet.

reviews.yes_case: Call Record Console turns the app into a dark-first practice console built on CRM-style record pages. Five objects (Persona, Scenario, Call Record, Rubric, Member) share one header and tab pattern, so the library, the live call and the debrief feel like one system. The live call is three zones on a dark canvas: a left rail with persona, buyer state, objection tags and a Geist Mono timer; a centre activity-timeline transcript with rubric hits pinned as teal markers and amber coach lines that collapse; and a right utility panel with a whisper card, next-question chip, objection alert, a Path tracker of talk-track stages and a live rubric meter whose bars link to evidence lines. The Path bar fills as the rep hits stages and is the same component before, during and after the call. The debrief mirrors that layout and shows an Estimate chip instead of a letter grade whenever heuristics were used, which fixes today's F from a keyword fallback. The library is a faceted rail with counts (job, industry, difficulty, objection, call type, source), saved views such as Ramp new hires, a sortable table with a card toggle, and a six-tab persona record page. The wizard is prompt-first, with provenance chips and a dry run before save. Models are named on the record (a Coach chip on the live console, a Graded by footer on every debrief), and a settings panel shows real OpenAI token and cost use. Against today's chat app and a three-item dropdown, this reads as a serious tool that sales organisations already know how to buy.
reviews.no_case: The Lightning frame is risky. It can drift into CRM clutter, and a Salesforce-shaped look-alike brings the trade-dress and naming questions the proposal itself lists. A dark console with three panels, record headers and Tremor dashboards may be too dense for a rep on a live call, and the density limit is a promise rather than a shown design. The 2.5 second cue cutoff means a slow coach silently drops its cues, so the live console can go quiet exactly when the rep needs it. The 24-job, 120-persona library is a content project that the proposal says must reach 80 personas before any public launch claim.

reviews.yes_case: Signal Coach is a total redesign on antd 5 with ConfigProvider tokens and the Ant Design X AI primitives (Bubble, ThoughtChain, Prompts, Sender, Suggestion, Think, Welcome, Conversations). Light is the default everywhere, and a dark cockpit is a separate mode via darkAlgorithm on its subtree, so the call reads as a focused space. The live cockpit has a top bar with the persona name, a Live dot, a JetBrains Mono timer, a cue-frequency chip and End and grade. The transcript is a Bubble list with the rep on the right and the persona on the left, with small coach tags under rep turns such as 'Good: asked budget' and 'Missed: next step'. A 360px right rail stays open with the current cue, a ThoughtChain showing why it fired, three next-best questions as Prompts, an amber objection alert with a suggested reply, and five live rubric bars labelled provisional. Every coach item shows its trigger quote, so reps can audit the coach before trusting it, and that is the signature move. The library opens with Prompts chips such as 'Insurance renewal, price objection', then a 260px facet rail and a card grid. The launch set is 120 personas built as 12 sales jobs by 10 industries with 10 per cell, so every filter returns something and empty cells show as a coverage map that invites contributions. The wizard streams its build as a visible ThoughtChain with source badges, auto-balanced rubric weights and a diff against the nearest template before Save, Export JSON or Open a contribution. Against today's chat app with no visible coach, this makes the AI work inspectable. For OpenAI, Realtime is the default voice transport, a settings panel picks the grader, coach and wizard models, and each output carries a provenance chip naming the model and prompt version, with Codex in PR review and release notes.
reviews.no_case: Default antd plus Ant Design X reads as enterprise admin, and the look score depends on a token and design pass the proposal has not yet done. Two styling systems are a real risk during migration: antd CSS-in-JS and Tailwind preflight can clash, and the plan wants the Tailwind component classes gone early. React 19 and Next 15 compatibility for antd and @ant-design/x is unverified and must be pinned before commitment. The live-route bundle needs strict lazy-loading discipline, and the XL effort runs a 120-persona content track in parallel. Coaching quality and latency, not layout, decide criterion D, and a strong cue panel with weak cues fails the baseline.

reviews.yes_case: Quiet Coach Console is a clean, copy-in Untitled UI React kit (React Aria accessibility, Tailwind v4.3) that gives a conventional but well-finished chrome: one primary action per screen, high-contrast forms, 16px inputs on phones to stop iOS zoom, and a dark live stage in both modes. The live call is a coach console with a talk-track stepper that ticks itself off, a speaker-turn transcript, a small SVG voice meter, typed cue cards capped at two visible, provisional rubric meters with evidence dots that jump to turns, and a coach level control (Silent, Light, Full). The library has a faceted rail with counts (role, industry, difficulty, objection, source), a recommended-for-your-role row, and Official and Community badges on packs. The wizard is a four-step stepper with source tabs (file, URL, paste, transcript), evidence chips, rubric weight sliders with a total check, and a 60-second test call before save. Compared with today's gradient-orb page and dropdown, it is a crisp, low-risk shell that a rep understands in a minute and a contributor can extend without learning a new system. The phased plan ships each step behind a flag with a visual regression pass.
reviews.no_case: It is the most conventional of the five, and the proposal says so: category C is self-scored 5. Untitled UI is widely used, so the chrome will look like many SaaS dashboards, and in a crowded category this does not earn a second look from OpenAI reviewers. The bespoke components that would keep the coach rail from looking templated are promised but not specified. The kit licence must be confirmed before vendoring, and the Tailwind v3 to v4 move in phase 0 adds churn across globals.css and the config before any user-visible gain.

reviews.yes_case: Live Desk Cockpit is a Catalyst-pattern app shell rebuilt from MIT parts (shadcn/ui, cmdk, Motion, Recharts), so it has a persistent sidebar with five groups, a collapsing icon rail, a Cmd-K palette and a four-item mobile tab bar, applied to every screen and licence-clean for an MIT repo. The live call is a dark three-zone cockpit: a 280px left rail with persona identity, goal and talk-track ticks; a centre with an SVG presence ring showing Listening, Persona speaking or Your turn, a transcript with objection chips, and a composer; and a 320px coach rail with up to three cue cards (whisper, objection alert), rubric meters that move from not started to partial to covered, and a pace gauge. The key trust rule is that a criterion turns to covered only when a transcript quote backs it, and cues go only to the rep, never to the persona or the audio channel. The landing page is the live cockpit itself, running as a looping SVG demo, with a model strip naming each OpenAI model and its job. The library is shelves by job family with See all, a filter rail with counts, and cards with a CI-checked badge meaning the pack passed schema and rubric-sum checks, across 120 personas and 60 scenarios. The wizard starts from one prompt box with source chips, offers numbered clarifying choice cards with Skip, shows a live preview, runs a 60-second test call, and then saves privately or opens a pull request. Compared with today's chat window and hidden talk-track drawer that gives no feedback, it shows what the coach sees and why, and it gives reviewers a clear path to contribute.
reviews.no_case: The shell is a known pattern rebuilt from parts, so the look depends entirely on execution, and a dark cockpit beside light pages can read as a generic admin app with one dark screen. The Catalyst licence point rests on Tailwind's blog text because the Catalyst page scrape returned 404, and the research was thin at 3 Mobbin and 2 Firecrawl searches. Live scoring (D) and the library (E) are conditional on per-turn scoring shipping and on at least 100 reviewed personas; without both, they fall below the 5.0 baseline. Dark and light QA doubles the work, and the amber and teal text on dark must be checked against WCAG AA before anyone trusts it.

reviews.yes_case: Copilot Rail Studio is a full-app redesign on shadcn/ui, Tailwind v4 tokens and Geist, with a dark live-call stage and a light default for the library, briefing, debrief, progress and team screens. On a call the transcript takes about 60 percent of the width, rep lines carry rubric chips such as 'Discovery +4', and a 360px copilot rail holds a Live estimate strip with five criterion bars and deltas, a talk-track stepper that ticks, up to three typed cue cards (objection, next question, whisper, guardrail) and a Whisper / Text only / Off switch. Every cue cites the turn and criterion it came from, 'Use line' drops the exact phrase into the composer without sending it, and the persona never sees cue text. The library is a faceted catalogue of 200-plus personas across about 18 job families, with live counts for role, industry, difficulty, objection type, call type and pack source. A five-step AI wizard takes a job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP or pasted call, drafts a schema-checked persona and rubric, runs a 60-second dry run and exports a pull request. Against today's three-item dropdown, chat-bubble call and blurry orb it is a complete change, and it names each OpenAI model where that model works, which speaks directly to the fund.
reviews.no_case: Its layout is the category default: a dark side rail beside the transcript is what Gong, Balto and Avoma already ship, so the idea is familiar and only the execution is new. The plan is XL, with nine screens, a rail, a wizard, a Tailwind 4 migration and a team view, and the proposal itself says the fund gets only phases 1 to 3. The 200-persona launch count is a content promise it scores at 6.5, and its D score of 7.0 depends on p50 cue latency under about 2 seconds, which has not been measured. The rail was built from competitor write-ups because Mobbin returned no live-coaching screens, so the cockpit's visual claims are untested.

reviews.yes_case: Call Cockpit Curriculum pairs a dark live cockpit with a curriculum-first front door. The left rail offers Learn (assigned paths and the next drill), Library, Practice, Progress and Team, with a New persona button and global Cmd-K. Paths are ordered curricula with certification gates and manager-assigned drills with due dates, so a three-item scenario dropdown becomes a programme a rep works through. Live, a left panel shows five criteria with 1-5 dot ratings and a live-estimate meter, the centre transcript carries violet cue chips under the rep's last line, and a right tray holds a next-best-question card, an amber objection alert and a talk-track stepper. A separate, cheaper coach stream reads each finished turn and returns rubric deltas with quotes, at most one cue and a next question, and never feeds the persona, so realism holds. The debrief becomes a navigable scorecard with a moment timeline, quote jumps and 90-second Replay-this-moment drills. On OpenAI, Realtime is a selectable voice engine beside ElevenLabs, a GPT-4.1-mini grader and a smaller GPT model drive cues, and Codex CLI is the contributor engine, with an AGENTS.md, a pack scaffold and Codex review of pack PRs. Call-centre and training-company buyers, which the F2 score points to, get the structure they already expect.
reviews.no_case: Cue pacing is the weak point on the baseline requirement. One cue per 25 seconds with a 12-second expiry means an objection that lands soon after a cue may get no alert, and the proposal never says whether objection alerts bypass that limit; its own D score is 5.5, only at the standard. Paths, certifications, assignments and a team roster form a second product on top of a live cockpit and 150 personas, making this the largest plan in the set and at risk of feeling like enterprise LMS software before a rep has practised a call. The violet-on-night palette is the generic AI-product accent, and keeping Tailwind 3 means the modern feel comes from tokens and a new shell rather than a visible stack upgrade.

reviews.yes_case: Call Record Console makes every object a Salesforce-style record. A live call is a Call Record with a Path bar of talk-track stages (Open, Diagnose, Qualify, Handle objection, Close) that fills as the rep reaches each one, and the same component appears before, during and after the call. The live screen is a dark three-zone console: a persona rail with buyer state and a Geist Mono timer on the left, a transcript where rubric hits pin as teal markers and coach lines sit inline in amber, and a utility panel with a whisper cue, next-question chip, objection alert and a live rubric meter whose bars link to evidence lines. The debrief uses the same record layout, so the keyword-fallback F becomes an honest Estimate chip, and every score and cue links to the exact transcript line. The library is 120 personas across 24 sales jobs with facets for job, industry, difficulty, objection type, call type and source, saved views such as Ramp new hires, a sortable table with a card toggle, and six-tab persona records. The wizard shows a source snippet on each generated field and ends in Save or Export as a PR-ready file. Models are named where they act (a Coach chip, a Graded by footer, a per-session cost panel), and records are planned to sync out to Salesforce or HubSpot, so the trainer sits inside the tools reps already use. That answers the F2 buyer, the sales org and the call centre, directly.
reviews.no_case: The look is modelled on Salesforce Lightning, and even without the logo, a record-page console reads as CRM admin software, so its distinctiveness borrows the category rather than inventing one. Coaching is only as good as the 2.5-second cutoff: a cue that arrives late is dropped, so a slow coach channel means a silent call, and no measured latency is given. The proposal rates its own library at 5.5 and will not claim a public library until 80 personas are seeded, so the content is still a promise. Five objects, dark consoles and a Tremor dashboard kit whose ownership and Tailwind 3 compatibility the proposal has not verified add integration and density risk to an XL plan.

reviews.yes_case: Warm Rehearsal is a calm, paper-and-terracotta redesign with a Dusk dark mode, Fraunces headings, Inter for UI and transcript, and a breathing presence ring that replaces the blurry orb and tracks the persona's audio level. Its distinctive mechanic is a 60-second breathing warm-up before each call, a 1-to-5 confidence check before and after the call, and a growth delta on the debrief, so the product measures how the rep feels as well as how they score. The live room is a presence ring, transcript with turn dividers, and a right rail with one whispered cue at a time (14 words or fewer, with a Why tap and a Quiet mode), a plum objection alert, a six-step talk-track ribbon and five live-read bars with trend arrows. The debrief leads with one takeaway sentence and one next-rep focus card, and tapping a quote replays that transcript line. The library is about 150 personas across 20 jobs with four facets, including Temperature (Warm, Warm-hot, Hot), and the wizard exports a PR-ready persona file. The OpenAI story is a Model lab that accepts any OpenAI-compatible base URL, a Realtime voice option beside ElevenLabs and a Codex-friendly repo. It looks nothing like today's generic Tailwind SaaS and is the most distinct design of the five.
reviews.no_case: Calm is the risk the proposal names itself: a serif paper palette and breathing rings read closer to a wellness app than to the cutting-edge AI voice coaching the brief asks for. Live scoring is hidden by design, with numbers off by default and cues at most once every 20 seconds, so the rubric reads mainly as trend arrows that meet the standard only just. The Hot tier that fixes the softness is a stated mitigation, not a designed screen. The shadcn primitive move from Radix to Base UI comes from a vendor blog the proposal itself marks unverified, and the Tailwind 4 migration touches every screen.

reviews.yes_case: Fluent Live Coach moves the whole app onto Microsoft's Fluent 2 component system (@fluentui/react-components v9 only), with a custom deep-teal brand ramp seeded at #0F766E, a violet coach accent kept apart from score and alert colours, and Griffel tokens and Fluent icons in place of the Tailwind component classes. Light is the default theme and the live call is always a dark stage. On the call, the persona avatar with a speaking ring, timer and mute sit on the left, a speaker-labelled transcript with beat tags such as 'Pricing: not yet' sits in the centre, and a right coach rail shows live rubric bars with change arrows, a talk-track progress list, one whisper at a time and an amber objection alert with a suggested reply. A separate coach call after each turn returns per-criterion deltas, talk-track state and objection flags, with a visible 'coach thinking' state rather than stale cues. The debrief is evidence-first, with a provenance chip naming the grader model and a warning when the keyword fallback ran. The library pairs a Tree facet rail with cards and a DataGrid list view. For buyers in Microsoft shops and sales ops, a Fluent system is familiar and reads as enterprise-ready, and the design carries an OpenAI model-role strip and an AGENTS.md with a Codex section.
reviews.no_case: A Fluent app reads as Teams or Office, which the proposal's own risk list admits, so I score its distinctiveness at 3 and its modern score at 4. It replaces the Tailwind-first styling the repo already uses with a second styling system, so the migration is a full rewrite with no modern-stack gain. The Fluent v9 React 19 peer range is unchecked and the token values come from an unofficial reference, while Segoe UI Variable is Windows-only and its Inter fallback has not been checked on macOS, Linux or Android. The persona library never states a launch count, only 'a launch set covering every job', and the 2-second coach target is untested, so on the proposal's own numbers E and D sit barely above the standard the brief sets.

reviews.yes_case: Warm Rehearsal turns the whole app into a calm practice room. It sits on a warm paper canvas (#FAF6F0) with terracotta primary actions, sage for strengths, honey for whispered coach cues and a Fraunces serif for titles and grade letters, plus a Dusk dark mode for night practice. The blurred orb becomes a breathing presence ring that tracks the persona's voice level. Every call opens with a 60-second warm-up and a 1-to-5 confidence check, and the post-call result is compared against it. On the live call, a right coach rail gives one whispered cue at a time (14 words or fewer, with a Why expander, fading after 8 seconds), plum objection alerts, a six-step talk-track ribbon, and five criteria as thin bars with trend arrows, with numbers hidden until toggled. Pause and breathe is free and never costs score. The debrief opens with one takeaway sentence beside a grade ring and growth delta, and any quote replays the exact transcript line. The library holds about 150 seeded personas across 20 jobs, filtered by job, industry, temperature (Warm, Warm-hot, Hot, which doubles as difficulty) and objection type, with a Cmd-K palette and a temperature bar on each card. The wizard takes five source types, drafts persona, scenario and rubric with a source line on every field, auto-sums rubric weights to 100 with a reason for each weight, runs a 30-second dry run, and exports a pull-request file. For the OpenAI fund it puts OpenAI in the product: a model chip with per-call cost, a Model lab that accepts any OpenAI-compatible base URL, Realtime as a voice provider beside ElevenLabs, and Codex-run PR review of persona files. Against today's dropdown, three cards and four numbers, every screen changes.
reviews.no_case: The calm palette is the proposal's own biggest risk. The research it cites says buyers in competing tools feel too agreeable and robotic, and a warm paper room with breathing rings can read as a wellness app rather than a serious cutting-edge AI product. It self-scores look and unique design at 7 with little beyond a palette to show for it. One cue every 20 seconds is a hard ceiling, so in a fast objection the rep waits 20 seconds for the next cue. A mandatory 60-second warm-up before every call adds friction for experienced reps. The Hot tier is the only answer to the realism critique, and it is one tier of pushback, not a full adversarial engine. The Tailwind 3 to 4 migration touches every screen, and the shadcn/Base UI primitive claim rests on an unverified vendor blog. The 150-persona library is a content project with no named owner.

reviews.yes_case: Fluent Live Coach gives the app one mature component system: FluentProvider with a custom teal brand ramp seeded at #0F766E, Griffel tokens and Fluent icons, so the look is consistent, enterprise-safe and accessible by default. The live call sits on a dark stage (#141414) so coaching colors stay readable. A left panel holds the persona avatar, speaking ring, timer, mic level and End. The centre transcript carries beat tags such as Discovery and Pricing: not yet. A right coach rail shows live rubric bars with change arrows, a talk-track progress list, one violet whisper cue at a time, and an amber objection alert with a suggested reply. The coach is specified more carefully than in most of the set. It must cite quotes for score changes above a threshold, shows a coach-thinking state rather than stale cues, targets about 2 seconds after the rep stops speaking, and falls back to scores only, with a visible notice, if the coach call fails. The debrief is evidence-first: a grader provenance chip (Graded by gpt-4.1-mini, 14 quotes), a score timeline whose markers jump to transcript lines, and an accordion per criterion. The wizard puts a why chip on every generated field linking to its source sentence. For enterprise sales organisations, a layout close to the Microsoft tools they already buy is a procurement advantage. Realtime as a first-class voice option, AGENTS.md and a Codex CLI section cover the OpenAI and contributor story. It beats today's chat app clearly on coaching and evidence.
reviews.no_case: It looks like Microsoft Teams or Windows enterprise software. That is the conventional look the brief grades low on look and unique design, and the custom teal ramp does not remove the Fluent silhouette. The proposal self-scores unique design at 5.5. Its own risks list says the product can read as Microsoft, and the mitigation is a color ramp and a README disclaimer, which is weak for an MIT open-source project. Segoe UI Variable is Windows-only, so macOS, Linux and Android users get Inter, which is not visually tested. The React 19 peer range for Fluent v9 and the token values, taken from an unofficial reference, are both unverified. The library promises every job but gives no count, so the persona scale is undemonstrated. Replacing Tailwind and every component class with Griffel is a full rewrite for a look that is less modern than the alternatives. Its own F1 self-score of 4 says the SaaS market is crowded, so the product has to win on fit, and this design does not win on look.

reviews.yes_case: Call Record Console is a dark-first console for AI sales practice, built as CRM-style record pages. Each persona, scenario, call record, rubric and team member is a record with the same header (avatar, name, role, difficulty, last score), tabs, related lists and a Path bar of talk-track stages (Open, Diagnose, Qualify, Handle objection, Close). The same Path component appears before the call, during it and after it, so the rep learns one visual language. The live call is a three-zone console on a dark canvas. A left persona rail shows buyer state and the timer. The centre transcript is an activity timeline where rubric hits pin as teal markers and coach lines sit inline in amber. A right utility panel holds a whisper cue card, a next-best-question chip, an objection alert, a Path tracker, and a live rubric meter whose bars link to exact evidence lines. Coach mode is Silent, Whisper or Full, and cues that arrive after 2.5 seconds are dropped rather than shown late, an honest rule the current app cannot offer because it has no coach. The library ships 120 personas across 24 sales jobs and 15 industries, filterable on six facets (job, industry, difficulty, objection type, call type, source), with saved views such as Ramp new hires and Pricing pushback. Each persona is one JSON file that contributors add by pull request. The wizard takes a URL, job description, CRM export, ICP or pasted call, fills persona, scenario and rubric with a source snippet on each field, and ends in a 60-second dry run before save or PR export. For the fund, models are named where they act: a Coach chip on the live console, a Graded by footer on every debrief, and a per-session token and cost panel. The Realtime voice engine is marked as not claimed until it ships. Every screen moves from the dropdown and orb to a coherent system.
reviews.no_case: Lightning-style density is the risk the proposal itself flags, and a record-page metaphor can make practice feel like CRM data entry, the opposite of the focus a rep needs before a call. Dark-first consoles are common in AI tools, so the distinctiveness sits in the information architecture more than in the visual. Borrowing Lightning's structure keeps the product close to an incumbent's shape, which weakens the brief's ask for cutting-edge unique design. Tremor, the dashboard kit, has an ownership claim and a Tailwind 3 compatibility question, both unverified, and the proposal depends on it for every KPI and trend chart. The 80-persona floor before any public claim means the library is still a content project. Syncing records to Salesforce and HubSpot is an enterprise integration that belongs after the core loop works.

reviews.yes_case: Signal Coach is an Ant Design X cockpit where the AI-native components carry the product. Bubble renders the transcript, Prompts offers next-best questions, Sender carries suggestion chips, and ThoughtChain shows why each cue fired. Every cue opens to the exact transcript line and the reasoning that triggered it, so a rep can check the coach before trusting it. Think shows while the coach works and never blocks the rep's next turn. The live call is a dark cockpit inside a light app: a top bar with persona, Live dot, timer and End and grade; a 360px right column with the current cue, three next-best questions, an amber objection alert, and a live rubric with five progress bars labelled provisional; and a bottom dock with Sender and mute. Criterion scores lock at debrief, which shows a score ring with a percentile line and a moment-replay timeline whose markers jump to transcript lines. Library filters live in the URL, so any filtered view can be shared. A coverage map shows empty job-by-industry cells and invites contributions to fill them, an idea no other proposal has. The wizard streams its build steps with sources visible, so an AI-generated persona is inspectable rather than a hidden form prefill. Settings picks the models for grader, coach and wizard, and each AI output carries a provenance chip naming its model and prompt version. A public grader-eval page comparing AI scores with human-labelled transcripts is a credible showcase for an open-source OpenAI project. Antd and Ant Design X are real, established libraries, and the plan deletes the Tailwind component classes so the app becomes one system.
reviews.no_case: Default antd reads as enterprise admin, and the proposal concedes that the look depends entirely on token work and a real design pass, so the shipped result may look like a back office, not a cutting-edge product. Compatibility of Ant Design X and antd 5 with React 19 and Next 15 is unverified, and antd's CSS-in-JS plus Tailwind preflight is a known clash during migration. Bundle weight on the live route is a real cost that lazy-loading only partly fixes. The library arithmetic does not add up: 12 sales jobs by 10 industries with 10 personas per cell is 1,200 personas, not the 120 claimed, so the content plan is internally inconsistent and a reviewer will catch it. Realtime as the default voice path is a large voice-pipeline change rather than a switch. Light pages with a dark cockpit may look split in use.

reviews.yes_case: Quiet Coach Console is a crisp, conventional product on a copy-in Untitled UI React kit with React Aria accessibility and Tailwind v4.3 tokens. The light canvas (#F8FAFC) keeps continuity with today, and the dark stage (#0B1220) gives the live call a low-glare canvas in both modes. Inter with Sora for H1 and H2 makes a legible system. The live call is a coach console: a left talk-track stepper that checks itself off, a speaker-turn transcript, an SVG voice meter, typed cue cards (two visible at most, older ones collapse into a count), a Next best question card that appears only when the rep goes quiet or skips discovery, and a provisional rubric whose evidence dots jump to the exact turn. Coach level (Silent, Light, Full) is set before the call and can change mid-call. The briefing offers likely objections with a short prep line each, and the debrief links the weakest criterion to a practice-next library persona. The library uses facets with removable chips, a recommended-for-your-role row, Official and Community badges, and a preview drawer, so a three-item dropdown becomes a browsable catalog. The wizard is a four-step stepper with source tabs and a 60-second test call before save. Old URLs redirect and every phase ships behind a flag. Every surface shows which OpenAI model did the work and what the call cost. It is the least risky shape to ship on time.
reviews.no_case: The proposal admits its generic-look risk and self-scores distinctiveness at 5. Untitled UI is a widely used template, so the product will look like many other SaaS tools, which falls short of the brief's ask for unique design that feels like cutting-edge tech. The copy-in license is unverified. The library has facets but no count, so the word large is not demonstrated. The product is conventional by its own description. Scope is XL, and the coach service and persona packs are the long pole that the visual work hides. In a crowded SaaS market, a look that matches every competitor's chrome gives no reason to pick this product over Second Nature, Hyperbound or Yoodli.

reviews.yes_case: Copilot Rail Studio is a dark live-call cockpit with a light default everywhere else. In the call, the transcript sits on the left as speaker-labelled rows with timestamps and rubric chips such as 'Discovery +4'. A 360px copilot rail on the right holds a live score strip (an overall estimate plus five criterion bars with deltas, labelled Live estimate), a talk-track stepper that ticks as steps are covered, and a stack of at most three cue cards. Each cue is one of four types (objection, next question, whisper, guardrail) with an icon and a text label, and cites the turn and rubric criterion that triggered it. 'Use line' drops the exact phrase into the composer for the rep to send; nothing auto-sends, and the persona never sees cue text. Outside the call, the library has a left facet rail (role, industry, difficulty, objection type, call type, pack source, each with live counts), job-family rows with View all, and cmd-K. The five-step wizard runs from 'what are you selling' through context tabs with source chips, an editable persona beside a JSON preview with a schema-valid badge, rubric weights that must sum to 100, a dry run, and then save-privately or export-as-pack-PR. In the debrief, a grader-source chip says plainly when the keyword heuristic produced the grade, evidence chips highlight the exact transcript line, and 'Retry from turn 8' branches the call from the missed objection. Why it beats today's app: the call is a chat-bubble transcript with no feedback until End, and the library is a three-item select. This shows coaching and scoring while the call happens, ties every number to a quote, and makes the library browsable. The OpenAI story is visible: a Realtime voice chip on the stage, gpt-4.1-mini on the coach and grader, a Models page that accepts any OpenAI-compatible base URL, and a contributor Codex CLI prompt. The stack is shadcn on Radix with Tailwind v4 tokens, Geist, Motion, cmdk, and one Zod schema shared by wizard, coach and grader.
reviews.no_case: It is the least distinctive of the three advancing options. A dark stage with a right-hand rail is the Gong and Balto pattern the proposal borrows from, so a reviewer sees a competent copy of the category rather than a new identity. The Tailwind v4 migration is labelled Phase 1 (S), which understates moving every hand-rolled class, and nine screens, a rail, a five-step wizard and a 200-persona seed set amount to an XL build presented as a short fund plan.

reviews.yes_case: Ambient Orb Call Room makes the app feel like a call. The live call is a full-viewport canvas. A WebGL orb (React Three Fiber with a custom shader and a CSS gradient fallback) sits at about 44vh and breathes with the speaker's audio level. A five-arc rubric halo wraps it, one arc per criterion, with arc length for coverage and colour for the score band. A dashed halo means a live estimate; a solid one means the full grader has run. Above the orb are a Geist Mono timer and a Your turn or Their turn pill. Below it, one Instrument Serif italic whisper card rises, is read once, and fades after six seconds. An objection turns the halo coral and adds a one-line pivot card. Chrome dissolves after three seconds without pointer or touch, leaving the orb, the timer and one whisper; the controls return on movement, and the transcript sits in a drag-up sheet. The same orb is the brand mark, the persona avatar and the debrief header. The library has 120 seeded personas across 14 sales jobs, with a left facet rail that shows counts, job-by-job sections with View all, a 3-second voice preview on each card, and a right sheet with the full brief and a Practice button. The co-pilot wizard streams a persona card as raw context arrives (job description, URL, CRM notes, a transcript); each field carries a source chip back to the pasted text, a duplicate check runs against the nearest library persona, and a 60-second test call finishes the job. Why it beats today's app: the live screen is a chat bubble with no in-call feedback and a blurry orb that signals nothing. This gives the rep one place to look, puts the rubric in view during the call, and gives the product an identity that video-avatar competitors do not have. The OpenAI stack is named on every screen with a provenance line: gpt-4.1-mini as coach and default grader, Structured Outputs for the wizard, an optional OpenAI Realtime voice path beside ElevenLabs, a cost-per-call panel, and a How this repo uses Codex page that shows real usage. Text mode stays on the same canvas with a smaller orb.
reviews.no_case: Its in-call scoring is the least legible of the three advancers. The rep sees five arcs and a colour band with no numbers and no criterion labels beside them, and the talk track is a row of progress dots, so the rubric is hard to read mid-call. Chrome-fade can hide evidence at the moment it matters, and the proposal's own self-score for live coaching is 5.4, just above baseline. The orb may also age faster than a plain tool, and the shader's CSS fallback is named but not designed.

reviews.yes_case: Pocket Coach Studio is a dark-first, phone-first progressive web app built on one rule: every primary action sits in the bottom 40% of a 390px screen. A four-item bottom tab bar (Practice, Library, Progress, Team, with a raised Start call button in the middle) and Vaul bottom sheets carry every secondary panel (talk track, rubric, persona detail, filters, coach history), so the rep never leaves the call. The look is a canvas of #0B0F14 with surfaces stepped up instead of blurred shadows, 1px hairlines, 20px sheet radii, Geist for text and Geist Mono for timers and scores, and one strict colour rule: amber always means the coach is speaking. On a phone, the live call is a 52px top bar (persona name, mono timer, state pill), a five-segment rubric strip where a hollow segment is a provisional score that firms up on the next turn, an auto-scrolling transcript, and a whisper card floating above an 88px dock of four 56px round buttons (mute, text, talk track, coach history) plus a press-and-hold End and grade. On desktop the same components become a three-column cockpit with a live rubric rail and coach feed. Each whisper is typed (next-best question, objection alert in rose, or talk-track step), carries a Why chip to the exact transcript line, and targets arrival about 1.5 seconds after the persona's turn, with a post-turn fallback. The library is about 150 schema-checked seed personas across roughly 25 industries, with facets for role, industry, difficulty, objection type, channel and language; each card is tagged Seed or Community and opens a sheet with Practice and Duplicate and edit. The wizard has four entry paths (paste a call, paste a job or ICP, import from a URL, describe it in a sentence), shows every generated field with a source-quote chip, runs a 60-second test call from the same card, and must pass the same schema as seed personas. Why it beats today's app: the current app is a desktop template with a three-item dropdown and no in-call feedback. This gives a clear coaching surface and a library that browses easily on a phone, and the library works offline. OpenAI is named throughout: a cue model chip on each coach card, graded-by on the debrief, generated-by on wizard output, Realtime as a voice option beside ElevenLabs, a tokens-per-call panel, a Models table in the README, and an AGENTS.md that lets Codex CLI add a persona and run the schema tests.
reviews.no_case: It makes the phone the primary surface for a product reps mostly use at a desk. Most of the brief's heavy screens (library browsing, the wizard's source-and-preview split, the team heat grid) are desktop-shaped, and the thumb-zone rule pushes them into sheets. The Vaul pin is a real maintenance cost, since shadcn's default drawer has moved to Base UI and the proposal must keep the Radix flavour on purpose. The offline library cache does little for a product whose calls need a live voice connection, and a dark, amber-accented mobile look is a familiar AI-app pattern rather than a new identity.

reviews.yes_case: Call Cockpit Curriculum treats practice as a programme. The Learn tab opens ordered paths and manager-assigned drills with due dates and pass thresholds. The Library browses about 150 personas across roughly 20 industries, with facets for role, industry, difficulty, objection type and call, and each pack shows its author, version and usage count. The wizard is source-first (job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP form or a pasted call), runs a dry run, and then saves privately or proposes the persona to a pack. The look is a warm-paper light default (#F7F6F2 canvas, white cards, hairline borders) with a night cockpit for the live call, one violet token reserved for every AI feature, and five-dot criterion ratings instead of raw bars. On desktop a slim left rail holds Learn, Library, Practice, Progress and Team, plus a persistent New persona button; on mobile a bottom tab bar has a centre Call button. The live call is a three-zone cockpit: a rubric panel of five criteria with 1-5 dots and live-estimate meters on the left, a transcript by speaker turn with violet cue chips under the rep's last line in the middle, and a right tray with the next-best question, an amber objection alert and the talk-track stepper. Debriefs add timeline markers, quote links that jump to the turn, a 90-second Replay this moment drill for weak criteria, a Better line rewrite and a certified or not-yet state. Why it beats today's app: a three-item dropdown becomes a catalogue a manager can assign from, and the existing orgs and supervisor notes finally get a UI. The OpenAI story is concrete: gpt-realtime as a selectable voice engine shown in the cockpit footer, a smaller GPT model for live cues, GPT-4.1-mini for grading and the wizard, and Codex as the contributor engine through AGENTS.md, scaffolded packs and PR review in CI. Keeping Tailwind 3 is a sensible risk call.
reviews.no_case: The cue rule is too slow for a live coach. One cue every 25 seconds that expires after 12 means an objection at second ten may get no cue at all, and the proposal's own live-coaching score is only 5.5 if latency holds. The visual language reads as an LMS, which loses on the look categories, and the strongest business idea (curricula and certification gates) is an enterprise feature set the brief does not ask for. XL scope on top of that, with a team MVP still to build, is a lot of surface for a volunteer repo.

reviews.yes_case: Warm Rehearsal is a calm practice room for hard calls. The palette is a paper canvas (#FAF6F0) with Fraunces for titles and grade letters, Inter for UI and transcript, terracotta primary (#B4502E), sage for strengths, honey for whispered coaching, plum for objections, and a Dusk dark mode that uses the same token names. The centrepiece is a presence ring that breathes on a 6-second inhale and exhale during warm-up and scales with the persona's audio level, replacing the blurry orb. Before each call a 60-second warm-up runs, with an optional recording of your opening line and a 1-to-5 confidence check. After the call the debrief leads with one takeaway sentence in Fraunces, a grade ring, the growth delta against your last attempt, and confidence before and after, so the product measures whether the rep got better and calmer. During the call one whispered cue shows at a time (14 words or fewer, in a honey card with a Why expander that fades after eight seconds), objection alerts use plum, a six-step talk-track ribbon checks off as steps are covered, and five criteria show as thin bars with trend arrows. Pause and breathe is free and never counts against the score. Evidence is quote-to-moment: tap a quote and the transcript replays that line. The library has about 150 seeded JSON personas across 20 jobs, a Temperature facet (Warm, Warm-hot, Hot) so a rep can pick a buyer who pushes back and interrupts, and a Community tab that credits authors. The wizard takes five sources and returns a persona, scenario and rubric with source lines and weights that auto-sum to 100, then runs a 30-second dry run and exports a PR-ready file. Why it beats today's app: the current app is a chat screen with a red End button and a dropdown, and this is the only one of the five that treats call anxiety as a product problem and measures it. The OpenAI story has a model chip with a per-call cost estimate on each call screen, a Model lab that accepts any OpenAI-compatible base URL and adds OpenAI Realtime beside ElevenLabs, and the wizard as the GPT flagship demo.
reviews.no_case: Calm is the wrong register for a brief that asks for modern, sleek, cutting-edge AI, and the proposal's own lens says calm must not mean soft, then leaves live scoring soft: numbers are off by default, cues come at most once every 20 seconds, and it relies on a Hot persona tier to answer the criticism that the buyer is too agreeable. Its claim that Radix is no longer maintained is unverified, and shadcn's current drawer docs still list a Radix flavour. The Tailwind 4 move touches every screen, and the risk list carries a pasted Mobbin usage banner, which suggests the research was not cleaned up.

reviews.yes_case: A whole-app rebuild on one token system: antd 5 with ConfigProvider tokens, Ant Design X for the AI-native parts, and the hand-rolled Tailwind component classes deleted rather than run beside it. The library is a light, filterable catalogue: checkbox facets synced to the URL, 120 personas across 12 sales jobs and 10 industries so every filter returns something, a persona sheet that plays the opening line, and a Build a persona action that opens a wizard whose ThoughtChain streams the build ('Read product page', 'Extracted 4 objections') and puts a source badge on every generated field. The live call is a dark cockpit, not a chat app: transcript bubbles beside a 360px coach panel that shows the current cue with a ThoughtChain of why it fired and the trigger quote, three next-best questions as Prompts, an amber objection alert, and provisional rubric bars that move as the rep talks. The debrief has a moment-replay timeline that jumps to the exact turn. OpenAI is visible as product, not a footnote: Realtime as the default voice path, a model and prompt-version chip on every AI output, Codex in the maintainer workflow, and a Built with Codex badge. Against today's app, which has a three-item dropdown and no coach, it covers every non-negotiable and looks like a modern AI product.
reviews.no_case: The Look score rests on token work that is not done yet: default antd plus Ant Design X reads as enterprise admin, and a fast port would be an admin panel with a dark mode. It is the heaviest stack in the set (antd, Ant Design X, G2 plots, Motion, a new icon set) on a live route that needs lazy-loading budgets, and the React 19 and Next 15 compatibility is unverified by the proposal's own admission. Ant Design X is young, so its API churn is a real maintenance cost for volunteer contributors. The risk list concedes that antd CSS-in-JS and Tailwind preflight will fight mid-migration. The XL plan runs five phases, a 120-persona content track and a voice-path change to Realtime at once, and the cue quality depends on a coach prompt the proposal does not design.

reviews.yes_case: A Catalyst-pattern app shell (persistent sidebar, collapsed icon rail, stacked mobile nav, clean page headers) built from MIT parts: shadcn/ui on Radix, cmdk for Cmd-K, Motion, Recharts and Geist. It is licence-clean for an MIT repo and keeps Tailwind 3.4, so the migration is incremental and the custom .card and .btn-primary classes are retired in place. Light pages cover library, pre-call, debrief, progress and team; the live call switches to a dark focus mode that reads as a separate stage. The call has three zones: a left rail with persona identity and talk-track ticks, a centre stage with a presence ring whose state pill says Listening, Persona speaking or Your turn, and a transcript with objection chips; and a right coach rail with up to three cue cards (whisper, objection alert), rubric meters that read not started, partial or covered, and a pace gauge. A criterion turns covered only when a quote backs it, and when the grader is down the rail shows a grey Heuristic badge instead of a stale number. The library has job-family shelves, facets for role, industry, difficulty, objection and channel, 120 personas and 60 scenarios, and a CI-checked badge on packs that pass schema and rubric-sum checks. The wizard is one prompt box with source chips, clarifying choice cards with Skip, provenance on each field, a 60-second test call, then save or open a PR. Codex has a concrete job: it reviews persona PRs for schema, rubric weights, objection coverage and tone, and posts a review comment. The landing hero is the live cockpit looping, so the product proves itself where today's blurry orb only decorates.
reviews.no_case: The sidebar-and-cards shell is the most copied SaaS pattern in the set, so distinctiveness is middling and the identity rests almost entirely on the dark stage. The pattern-not-code move means a custom AppShell has to be designed well, or the result is shadcn defaults with a sidebar. Dark cockpit plus light pages doubles visual QA and needs AA checks on amber and teal text. The Catalyst licence point rests on Tailwind's blog text, since the proposal's own page scrape returned a 404. The D and E scores are conditional on per-turn scoring shipping and on at least 100 reviewed personas, which are engineering and content risks no layout can fix. The 'Build a persona with Codex' page is named without a spec, so part of the fund story is still a label. It is a well-built product shell, not a visual statement.

reviews.yes_case: One design system from end to end: a single Radix Themes Theme (teal accent, slate gray, medium radius) with Radix primitives under the custom coaching HUD, so focus, keyboard and ARIA come by default and styling debt stays low. Light pages cover library, debrief, progress and team; a dark stage carries the live call and the landing hero. The call is a three-column cockpit: a persona with a state chip and voice ring, a transcript with speaker lanes and inline tags for objection, pricing and next step, and a coach rail with one whisper at a time, each quoting the exact transcript line it reacted to. The talk track ticks itself off, and a rubric criterion moves from tentative to confirmed only on two spans or one strong span, so the live score never overstates. The library is 120 seeded personas across the 14 sales jobs, with facets for job, industry, difficulty, objection type and channel, stored as JSON and validated by zod in CI. The wizard runs Source, Extract, Shape and Dry run, with streaming field cards, evidence snippets, confidence chips and a 90-second test call before it publishes locally or opens a PR. The fund story is the most concrete of the lower group: Realtime as a named voice provider beside ElevenLabs, a model label on every call, per-call cost in Settings, a Grader Lab that compares rubric agreement across models and takes contributor eval cases, and an AGENTS.md for Codex contributors. Against today's app it turns a chat screen into a cockpit and a three-item dropdown into a catalogue of real size.
reviews.no_case: This is the least distinctive look of the three advancing: Radix Themes is an elegant default with one teal accent, and the proposal's own risk list says reviewers may still read it as a template. Its coaching has the thinnest cue set of the three advancing: a single whisper and objection alerts, with no explicit next-best-question card or pace prompt, so it covers only part of the brief's list. The library and coach only reach baseline once the 120 personas are written and reviewed, which the proposal scores below 5 without them, so the content gate decides more than the UI. Radix Themes has no coaching HUD, score ring or persona dossier, so the low-debt pitch is partly false because the signature pieces are built from primitives anyway. Tailwind is removed last, which means a long stretch with two styling systems. Codex appears only as AGENTS.md and a conditional badge, not as a running PR review.

reviews.yes_case: The theme is the spine: each sales job (SDR cold call, insurance, solar) is a daisyUI data-theme skin scoped to its subtree, so the library cards and the call re-tint by job, while the reserved semantic colours (amber for coach cues, rose for objections, teal for live, violet for AI) stay fixed in every skin, so amber always means coach. Users switch Signal (dark), Ledger (light) or Contrast (AAA), and the manager view is pinned to Ledger because dense data reads better there. The live call gets the full cue taxonomy the brief asks for: Next question, Objection alert, Talk-track step and Pace warning, each citing transcript line IDs and accepted or dismissed with keys 1 and 2, with all five criteria re-scored after every rep turn. The debrief has a moments timeline where a click highlights the exact transcript line, and an 'Estimated: keyword fallback' state that replaces a yellow banner. Community skins and personas are small schema-checked files, and a Make a skin flow with a live contrast checker and a Propose to community button gives contributors a visible role. It is the cheapest migration in the set, staying on Tailwind 3 with daisyUI and mapping current tokens in Phase 0, and it is the most memorable of the five.
reviews.no_case: Per-job skins are a playful answer to a serious sales-coaching product, and the proposal's own risk list calls it skin sprawl: every skin multiplies QA and contrast checks. The library is 60-plus seeded personas, about five per sales job, well short of the large browsable catalogue the brief asks for, and the E case is conditional on content that has not been written. Realtime is never named, so the voice showcase the OpenAI fund reviewers would look for is missing. The Codex line is a vague promise of PR review and maintainer automation with nothing running, and the OpenAI attribution is deliberately modest, which weakens the fund pitch. The look is dark-first with a glass header and a mesh gradient, a dated AI-product aesthetic, and the proposal says its D score falls below baseline unless the coach lane ships.

reviews.yes_case: A copy-in SaaS kit (Untitled UI React on React Aria and Tailwind v4.3) gives crisp, conventional chrome with one primary action per screen and accessible behaviour built in: a combobox for persona search, listbox facets, a dialog for the wizard and a keyboard palette. Practice runs as one flow with a step bar (pre-call briefing, live call, debrief), and Create sits in the top nav as the AI wizard. The live call is a private coach console: a talk-track stepper on the left that ticks itself off while the caller is still talking, a speaker-turn transcript with an SVG voice meter, and a coach rail with a Next best question card, up to two stacked cue cards and provisional rubric meters with evidence dots that jump to the turn. The debrief becomes a scorecard with a Practice next card that opens the library persona for the weakest criterion. The library offers a Recommended for your role row, facets with counts and removable chips, a preview drawer and a Create a persona empty state. It is the least risky to build and the easiest for contributors who already know Tailwind and React Aria, and it shows the model and per-call cost on each surface. Against today's app it turns a dropdown and a chat screen into a console and a faceted catalogue.
reviews.no_case: The palette is nearly today's palette (canvas #F8FAFC, brand blue #1D4ED8, Inter, a near-identical ink), so the visible change is mostly layout and components, which is weak for a total redesign. The proposal's own C score is 5 and it admits Untitled UI is widely used, so reviewers will read it as a template, which is the exact problem the brief asks to fix. The open-source library is not sized: there is no launch count and no persona target, only a 'full open-source catalog', so the E case rests on content the proposal never commits to. The copy-in licence is unverified, and Base UI as the fallback would mean building the whole look in-house. The OpenAI angle is the thinnest of the five: Realtime is 'engineering work, not in the repo today' and Codex PR review is only a conditional README line. It reads as a conversion page for a SaaS product, not an AI coaching product.

reviews.yes_case: Live Desk Cockpit is a full app shell: a persistent left sidebar grouped into Practice, Library, Progress, Team and Settings, a top bar with Cmd-K, Start call and a theme toggle, and a four-item bottom tab bar with a More sheet on phones. Light surfaces (canvas #F6F7F9, white cards, hairline borders, Geist type) carry the library, pre-call, debrief and dashboard. The live call switches to a flat dark cockpit with three zones: persona identity, goal and talk-track ticks on the left; a centre stage with an SVG presence ring and a state pill (Listening, Persona speaking, Your turn); and a right coach rail holding up to three cue cards (whisper, objection alert) plus rubric meters per criterion that move from not started to partial to covered, with covered only when a verbatim quote backs it. It beats today's app because the call reacts while the rep is talking instead of after, the debrief becomes a navigable scorecard with quote links, and the library is a browsable catalogue of about 120 personas in job-family shelves with a filter rail, CI-checked badges and Cmd-K search. New with AI opens an eight-step wizard where every drafted field has a provenance chip pointing to its source sentence, and the rubric must sum to 100 before save. It looks like a current AI product rather than a stock template, and the OpenAI story is on screen: model chips in the cockpit, a Settings > Models page with each model's job and per-call cost, Realtime as a selectable voice engine, and a Build a persona with Codex page that produces schema-valid JSON.
reviews.no_case: The shell is a shadcn/Catalyst-shaped sidebar with white cards and a blue primary, which is close to the default SaaS template the brief calls generic. The dark cockpit panel is doing most of the work on distinctiveness. The claim that Catalyst licensing forces this route rests on Tailwind blog text, because the Catalyst page scrape returned 404. Per-turn GPT-4.1-mini scoring and cue calls add latency and cost on every rep turn. The D (5.6) and E (5.3) scores only clear the 5.0 baseline if per-turn scoring actually ships and about 100 personas get human review, and the proposal admits that. The Codex-checked PR review path is a plan, not a working workflow, so the fund angle is partly aspirational. It also stays on Tailwind 3, so the Tailwind 4 move is deferred rather than solved.

reviews.yes_case: Signal Skins Console is a daisyUI-based console where each sales job gets its own skin: SDR cold calls in orange, insurance and mortgage in indigo, home services and solar in lime. Each skin is scoped to that persona's subtree with data-theme, so the orb, cards and buttons re-tint with the job. The coaching colours never change across skins (amber means coach, rose means objection, teal means live, violet means AI), so a rep learns the signal language once. Users switch between Signal (dark, default), Ledger (light, used for the manager view) and Contrast (AAA), and every skin is checked for AA text contrast in CI. The live call has an amber whisper card with keys 1 and 2 to accept or dismiss that collapses to a chip after 12 seconds, five rubric rings that tick with delta arrows, and a rose objection alert with a one-line suggested reply. The debrief has a clickable moments timeline that highlights the matching transcript line. It beats today's app on identity: the library is a faceted, job-grouped card grid with a right drawer, and community contributions are a theme file or persona JSON checked by CI with a live contrast checker. That makes a first pull request a small, clear task. The OpenAI credit is a modest text attribution, and a developer event-log drawer shows the realtime event stream.
reviews.no_case: The skin-per-job idea is memorable, but it multiplies QA: eight skins at launch, each needing contrast and visual checks, and a community skin can still look wrong even when it passes AA. The coaching is the weakest part of the basic needs. D is self-scored at 5.3 and only clears baseline once the coach lane ships, so until then the live screen is a themed layout, not coaching. The library launches with 60-plus personas against the brief's 120-plus, and the curation takes weeks. daisyUI 4 is pinned, and the later daisyUI 5 move requires Tailwind 4, so the project would face a second migration. Re-tinting the call screen to each persona risks making a sales-training tool feel like a theme gallery, and reviewers may read it as cosmetic. The Codex fund angle is thinner than the others because it never names a concrete Codex workflow.

reviews.yes_case: Radix Coach Stage is one Radix Themes system: a single Theme (teal accent, slate gray, medium radius) wrapped around the whole app, with Radix primitives under every interactive piece. Light surfaces cover Library, Debrief, Progress and Team. The live call and landing hero use a dark stage with solid panels. Its best idea is cited whispers: every coach cue must quote the transcript line it reacted to, so the rep can check the coach. Rubric criteria move from tentative to confirmed only when evidence supports them, so the live score never overstates. The wizard runs Source, Extract, Shape and Dry run, with streaming field cards that show evidence and a confidence chip, rubric sliders that normalise to 100, and a 90-second dry run before publishing or opening a prefilled PR. It beats today's app because keyboard, focus and ARIA behaviour come from Radix, the migration is phased and screenshot-diffed, and the debrief pairs evidence quotes with a sticky transcript and a model receipt (grader model, latency, cost). The OpenAI story is concrete: Realtime as a voice provider, a Grader Lab that compares rubric agreement across models, and a Settings > Models page with cost.
reviews.no_case: It looks like a default Radix Themes app, which the proposal itself admits and which the brief calls generic. The dark stage and teal accent do not change the basic silhouette, so category C (unique design) is weak. Library and hero are sensible but unremarkable. Tailwind is kept until the final phase, so preflight and token clashes with Radix have to be managed for weeks. The realised E score (5.2) sits below 5 until the 120-persona library ships, and there are three built-ins today. Radix Themes has no coaching HUD, so the coach rail is custom work on primitives anyway. The business case is crowded (F1 4), and the open-source core only earns money through hosted features.

reviews.yes_case: Patch Bay Console treats the live call as an instrument. Everywhere else it is a calm bone-coloured app with hairline borders and the same tokens. On the call it becomes a graphite console: a coach-intensity knob (Off, Hints, Full) that visibly changes how often the coach speaks; six talk-track step keys that latch lit when the grader marks a step covered; a rubric rack of five channel strips with coverage meters and covered, partial or missed LEDs; a 12-LED voice-level ring; and a cue strip with a green, amber and red LED language plus a Coach me key. Every status pairs LED colour with a glyph and a text label, so nothing depends on colour alone. Motion is short and mechanical (knobs settle in about 120ms, step keys latch in 60ms), and reduced motion becomes instant colour change. It beats today's app because it is the most distinct of the five: a chat screen with a hidden talk-track drawer becomes something the rep operates, and the library and debrief stay on paper so dense reading is not skeuomorphic. The OpenAI story is credible: a model ledger on every debrief showing which model graded, token counts and estimated cost; a bring-your-own-key setting for any OpenAI-compatible base URL with gpt-4.1-mini as default; a Realtime voice toggle; and a Contribute button that exports persona JSON, plus a /contribute page of good-first-persona issues.
reviews.no_case: It is the riskiest look in the set. Tactile hardware can read as novelty, and the only test planned is a five-rep check. The custom instrument kit (knob, LED ring, LED bar, channel strip, step key) is new SVG code that needs full keyboard and screen-reader support, which is heavy build and QA work before a screen ships. The library targets about 240 personas but launches with 60, and persona quality is a content project. Cue quality is unproven, so cues default to off until a labelled eval set exists, which leaves D at baseline on day one. The design also runs two visual languages (hardware on the call, paper everywhere else), so the total-UI change is less coherent than the others. The Tailwind v4 move is layered on top of all that. Competitor claims come from vendor blogs and are unverified.

reviews.yes_case: Signal Room Mission Control is a dark-by-default instrument console. It has a slim icon rail (Practice, Library, Progress, Team), a Cmd-K palette across personas, calls and settings, and a header with the org switcher and active voice mode. The live call looks like a telemetry console on a near-black canvas: a left rail with the call clock, a talk-ratio gauge that turns coral after 20 seconds above 70 percent, a words-per-minute gauge and a tone bar; a centre speaker-lane transcript with per-turn waveforms drawn on canvas; and a right coach rail that shows one amber cue at a time with checkpoints that tick off. Rubric meters stay tentative until a verbatim quote confirms them. The debrief replaces the long scroll with a waveform where each criterion score is an evidence tick you can replay, and a synced transcript docks beside it. The library is a three-column card grid with multi-select facets that are shareable in the URL. The wizard drafts from a URL, document, transcript or form, cites a source line for each field, and runs three simulated calls to flag flat or unrealistic replies before saving. It beats today's app because the call shows what is happening and why, the light theme is designed at equal weight for calm reading, and the OpenAI models are visible on every call through a model-stack strip with latency and cost per model. The Codex angle is also practical: AGENTS.md and token docs let Codex CLI change the UI safely, and Codex PR review can check gallery snapshots.
reviews.no_case: Dark telemetry can read as a trading terminal and feel cold to new reps, and the light theme is promised but not yet shown. This is XL work: a Tailwind v4 move plus Base UI, both recent and churn-prone, plus a new shell, so phase 1 has several moving parts before any user sees value. The proposal is internally inconsistent on timing: the coach runs on 8 to 12 second windows, but the target is a cue within two seconds of the rep's turn ending, and the document does not reconcile the two. The waveform-based evidence assumes per-turn audio is kept and replayable. The brief does not show the app retaining audio, and retention brings consent and storage obligations. The coach channel does not exist, so the live console is a shell until it is built. Nine screens plus a coach channel and a team backend is a lot for an open-source project, as the proposal itself admits.

reviews.yes_case: Signal Room Mission Control redesigns all nine screens around one dark instrument grammar, with a light theme designed at equal weight rather than inverted. The live call is a three-zone telemetry console. The left rail holds the call clock, a talk-ratio gauge that turns coral after 20 seconds above 70 percent, a words-per-minute gauge, a tone bar, and live rubric meters that stay marked tentative until a verbatim quote confirms them. The centre is a speaker-lane transcript with per-turn waveforms drawn on canvas from the audio analyser. The right coach rail shows one amber whisper cue at a time, with the exact next question as ghost text, plus coral objection chips and checkpoints that tick off. The persona channel only talks, and a separate coach channel emits typed events, each rendered in exactly one place, so the persona never breaks character. The library is a facet rail (sales job, industry, difficulty, objection type, call type, voice or text) with counts, multi-select filters shareable in the URL, and job-family pills for 12 to 15 sales jobs. Forks export as PR-ready files. The AI wizard takes a URL, document, transcript or form, streams each field in with a citation to its source line, stress-tests the draft with three simulated calls, and can export as a pull request. Every call shows a model strip naming which OpenAI model handled voice, coaching and grading, with latency and cost. Against today's app, which is a chat window with no feedback, a three-item select and a hand-typed persona form, this turns the product into a coached cockpit with a browsable library and a wizard that shows its sources. The phased plan keeps every route and imports old saved scenarios.
reviews.no_case: It is a trading terminal in a sales tool. Its own risk list warns that dark telemetry can feel cold to new reps, and the calm light theme is asserted, not tested. The live-scoring score (D 5.8) rests on a coach channel that does not exist yet, so the two-second cue promise and the gauge-heavy left rail are still design on paper. Nine screens, a canvas waveform, Motion, Recharts and a shadcn/Base UI migration is an XL rewrite for an open-source project that needs contributors to join quickly.

reviews.yes_case: Broadcast Desk treats each practice call as a live stream. The persona sits as an audio-reactive ring on centre stage, with live captions as a lower third and a talk-track segment bar. A coach chat feed on the right shows typed cue cards with glyphs (amber nudge, rose objection alert, violet next question, green praise), and each card links to the transcript quote that triggered it. A left scoreboard shows five criteria with provisional bars and green or rose delta chips. When a call ends, the debrief is a replay-first timeline with coach markers and three auto-marked clips (Best moment, Missed fee question, Strongest close), each playable and exportable as a 1200 by 630 moment card for sharing. Persona cards carry a 10-second Hear them voice sample, so a rep can judge a persona before picking it. The library sits on a calm light surface with a filter rail, collections such as Insurance renewals, and 150-plus personas across 20-plus sales jobs. The wizard drafts from a job description, product URL, CRM notes or a pasted call, shows a provenance chip on every field, and requires a 60-second test-drive call before saving. A Model rack in the footer and Settings names the OpenAI model for each role (Realtime as a selectable voice engine, GPT-4.1 family for coaching, grading and the wizard), with per-call token counts and cost. Against today's three-item dropdown, blurry orb and stacked chat, this is a product people can watch, share and use as a team's practice record.
reviews.no_case: The stream and clip metaphor is the one choice its own risk list says can read as gamey to the sales-leader buyers it wants. The coach rail is still a chat feed with cards, which is the pattern the brief calls out as the problem. Auto-clips, moment-card exports and a 10-second voice sample for every one of 150-plus personas add production and voice cost the proposal does not budget, and cues can land 1 to 2 seconds after the moment has passed. Its D and E self-scores are both 6.0, so the coaching and library are only just above baseline.

reviews.yes_case: Flight Deck Cockpit mirrors the rep's real loop as three screens in one instrument grammar. The pre-flight brief is a checklist of status lamps for mic level, persona loaded, goal read and talk track reviewed. Start flight enables only when the mic and goal lamps are green, and objection cards show the trap and a prep answer before the first word. The in-call HUD keeps a flight log of the transcript in the centre. Six rubric tape gauges on the left move after every turn with a tally such as Discovery 3 of 10. A right stack of at most two coach cue cards gives each cue a one-tap Use line that drops the suggested phrase into the input. Cues are throttled to one per 20 seconds and expire after eight seconds, and a grader sidecar keeps live numbers and the final grade on the same rubric. The debrief is a black box: a scrubbable timeline of the whole call with a score curve and event markers, where the gauges rewind as the audio replays and evidence chips seek to the exact second a quote was said. The dark cockpit is the default for flight and debrief, while daylight covers the library, wizard, logbook and team, all from one token file. The library is faceted by role, industry, difficulty, objection and mode, with usage counts (flown N times) and a Create with AI tile. The wizard streams fields with confidence chips and gates saving behind a two-minute test flight. Each flight report names the OpenAI model behind each job (GPT-4.1-mini for grading and cues, Structured Outputs for the wizard, Realtime as a selectable voice), with a cost estimate. An amber Estimate lamp shows when a heuristic fallback replaces a graded score. Against today's chat app, scroll-only debrief and four-number dashboard, this is the only proposal where every screen has one named job and a clear next action.
reviews.no_case: The aviation theme is a costume over an XL build. The live HUD depends on a per-turn grader sidecar that does not exist yet, and its own self-scores (D 6.5, E 6.5) hold only if it is built exactly as designed. Dark cockpit, tape gauges and flight-log language risk reading as a theme park to enterprise sales buyers, and six moving gauges plus a cue stack can crowd a rep who is already talking. Rewriting every screen from Tailwind 3 to 4 while also adding a grader, a replay engine and a manager view is a lot of parallel risk.

reviews.yes_case: Swipe-to-Rehearse Coach Studio is a dark-first live call with a clean three-zone layout. A left talk-track rail ticks as steps are detected, a centre transcript stream has speaker labels and mono timestamps, and a right coach panel holds stacked live rubric meters with delta chips, one whisper card at a time, an objection alert banner, a talk-to-listen ratio meter and a cost-per-call ticker in the footer. The coach is a separate model stream, so the persona never sees coaching, and whispers auto-dismiss after eight seconds. On phones the coach is a bottom sheet with peek, half and full snap points, a rubric dot strip and a long-press End. The library defaults to a filterable grid with a sticky rail for job, industry, difficulty, objection and mode, saved filter sets, Built-in and Community badges and a My library tab. That fits the finding that people compare dozens of options in grids. A deck mode turns objection drills into an opt-in quick habit (swipe right to run, left to skip, up to save). The four-step wizard takes any source, drafts persona, scenario and rubric through structured outputs, shows a provenance badge, runs a dry run and exports the same file format for contributions. Playwright screenshots of all screens in both themes become the regression baseline. Against today's cramped chat layout and three-item dropdown, it is the most conservative and most buildable of the five.
reviews.no_case: It is the most conventional of the five.
