The wizard has the strongest grounding story in the set: it lists what it found in the source with quote chips before drafting any field, then marks each generated field as quoted or inferred in amber. The library is 200 persona-and-scenario pairs in 20 industry packs, each pack a folder contributors can PR. Each persona is a zod-validated JSON file that doubles as the OpenAI Structured Outputs schema. Against today's app, a template look with a select and no feedback, it gives reps visible scoring during the call and a debrief that says whether a model or a heuristic graded it. For the fund, every AI output carries a provenance chip with model and latency, and cost per session shows on the dashboard. It stays on Tailwind 3 with shadcn, so the build risk is low.
reviews.no_case: Monochrome reads cold to a sales audience, and as a Vercel-derived look it is the least original of the five. The proposal's own distinctiveness score (C 6.5) says as much, and a fund reviewer may see a dev-tool clone and remember nothing. The Geist font licence is unverified. For an MIT open-source release that is a blocker, not a footnote, and the proposal lists it only as a risk. The live coach makes a structured gpt-4.1-mini call per caller turn with a two-second p50 target, which roughly doubles per-turn API cost. The spend cap is planned, not designed. The 200-persona launch target is a content project with no seed-quality plan, so the E score (6.5) rests on content that does not exist yet. Keeping Tailwind 3 defers the v4 move, which means token and component work will be partly redone later. Selling to entities (F2 6.5) depends on enterprise features (SSO, SCIM, SOC 2) that the core product does not provide.

reviews.yes_case: Cockpit is a dark, keyboard-first control room built on shadcn/ui over Radix. Dark is the default, with a full light token set at parity for bright rooms. Cmd-K drives every screen and every command shows its keycap, so the palette teaches the shortcuts. The left rail is 48px icons that expand to labels, and the mobile bottom bar keeps visible navigation, so the palette is an accelerator rather than a gate. The signature is density split by job: dense tables with hairline rules for the library, progress and team, and a sparse live call. The library is a keyboard-row table (j, k, Enter, slash to search) with a faceted rail that shows counts, a grid toggle and a preview drawer with Practice, Duplicate and Edit on GitHub. The live call uses resizable panes: a transcript in two speaker lanes with inline marks, a talk-track rail, and a coach stack showing at most one amber whisper cue plus an objection alert. Eight rubric meters stay provisional until two turns of evidence exist. The top bar carries a presence ring, a mono timer, the live coach latency and End and grade. The debrief is a split view, with the report on the left and a sticky transcript on the right. Every number links to its quote, and a provenance chip says whether a model or the heuristic graded the call, which turns today's silent fallback into a labelled state. The team view uses the org, team and supervisor-note data the app already has, with a heatmap and an assign drawer. Live meters and the final score share the debrief grader, so they agree by construction. It is the most credible build here: every component is a known library, Tailwind 3 stays, and it can ship in phases with the old routes kept. For the fund, the readout names the Realtime voice, coach and grader models, the Structured Outputs badge marks validated output, and AGENTS.md is written for Codex CLI. Against today's chat app and blurry orb, it reads as a professional tool.
reviews.no_case: It is the most familiar look here. Dark, Linear-style, command-palette software is now a default for developer and AI tools, so the first screenshot may look like many other products, and the distinctiveness score (5.5) is the honest answer. Cmd-K-first suits power users, but a rep on a call is not a keyboard power user, and dense tables are hard to read for a non-technical rep. The single-cue rule is disciplined, but it makes the coaching feel quiet rather than alive. D (6.0) holds only if the coach stream gets built, and the proposal says the UI alone would score about 5. The library needs roughly 120 reviewed pairs. Below about 60 at launch, E falls under the bar, so the content plan is the real launch risk. Dark-first can hurt readability in bright rooms, which the proposal names but does not resolve. Pinning Radix on purpose is defensible, but it means the team forgoes later shadcn component improvements. Selling to entities (F2 7) depends on manager features the proposal leaves largely unbuilt.

reviews.yes_case: Coach's Field Notebook is a warm paper-and-ink training notebook. The page is paper (#F4EEE1) with a faint grain, cards are index cards with a 2px radius and a ruled top line, and the coach writes in vermilion Caveat handwriting in the margin beside each transcript line. A live call is an open spread: the transcript on ruled lines with rep lines in blue ink and caller lines in graphite, and a right page with the coach margin, a live rubric ledger with pencil bars and talk-track ticks. Objections appear as tilted yellow sticky notes linked to the talk-track step. The grade lands as an ink stamp tilted a few degrees. Every number in the debrief is tied to a quote and a transcript line, so the scorecard reads like a marked-up record of the call. That is the easiest traceability story to explain to a reviewer. The library is the one part that drops the texture for a crisp grid with job-family index tabs across the top, which keeps the rep oriented to the sales job. The wizard uses a six-step left rail, a live index card that fills in as the model streams, and a 60-second test roleplay before save. Against today's blurry orb and generic feature cards, the landing page shows a product-real spread with coaching and grading on the first screen. It is the most distinctive proposal in the set (C 8.5). The README reuses the hero with a How it uses OpenAI diagram. Settings lists the model for each role with an override for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so forks can swap models. AGENTS.md and a proposed Codex skill that drafts persona packs give contributors a clear way in.
reviews.no_case: Warm paper and handwriting read as retro or twee, and the proposal admits the risk. The brief asks for modern, sleek and cutting edge. A grain-textured notebook with a handwriting face on the coaching voice is a hard sell to enterprise buyers and to a fund reviewer scanning for AI-era polish, and its modern score (6.5) is the weakest of the top group. Caveat at 20 to 22px for coach notes is a legibility and accessibility risk at exactly the moment a rep needs to read fast. Mixing two type voices on one screen adds visual noise. Lamp-lit dark mode and the print styles widen what has to be maintained. The 1.5-second live-coach target is only as good as the coach stream, and the proposal says the design meets the standard only if that stream ships. The shadcn-on-Base-UI default claim comes from a third-party blog, so the stack choice rests on an unverified premise. The library is a crisp grid, so the notebook identity stops at the library door, and reviewers may read that as a split personality. Selling to entities (F2 6) is weaker, since the look is the least enterprise-ready of the five.

reviews.yes_case: Clearcall Coach Console is a high-contrast, screen-reader-first coaching console. The canvas is warm off-white (#F7F7F4) with ink text at 18.7:1 on white, controls have 3:1 edges, targets are 44px and live-call controls 56px, and text scales to 200 percent with no horizontal scroll. Motion is off under reduced motion, and every state is shown as text and icon, so colour is never the only signal. The live call has three named landmark regions (Transcript, Coach, Controls) and a talk-track rail whose steps read Done, Next or Missed. Rubric rows show points, a bar and a status word, tagged Provisional until a grader confirms them. One cue at a time appears with a type label (Ask, Objection, Next question) and a Dismiss button, and a single polite announcement is queued at most once every eight seconds. The S key reads the full score aloud on demand. The library is grouped into sales-job packs with four facets, shown as a checkbox rail and as removable chips, and every card has a 30-second voice preview. The wizard asks one question per step with a labelled progress bar and shows the source sentence behind each extracted field (product, buyer, objections, price band), all editable. The debrief uses icons and words for grade and goal status, plus evidence chips that jump to the transcript line. Against today's app it adds the manager surface, a forced-colours path and a live call that works for people who cannot read a small orb. An axe-core WCAG AAA gate on every pull request is a credible signal to contributors and reviewers. Enterprise buyers such as BPOs, training firms and call centres often treat accessibility as a procurement requirement, which is the F2 case. For the fund, each debrief carries a model receipt, a Model lab page grades the same transcripts with gpt-4.1-mini and gpt-4.1 side by side, and Codex reviews persona and rubric pull requests.
reviews.no_case: It is the most conservative look here. Clean, high-contrast and accessible is a rigour strength, but the result could be any well-built SaaS app, so the fund reviewers get little to remember, and the look (A 7) does not clearly meet a brief that asks for cutting edge. AAA contrast and 44px targets limit brand character and crowd the mobile live call, as the proposal admits. The screen-reader cue cadence is a guess until blind and low-vision users test it, and cues stay opt-in until then, so the live-coaching behaviour is not yet settled. The OpenAI Realtime voice provider has to be built, because voice runs on ElevenLabs today. The Model lab page is a second product surface to build and maintain. Manager views of individual call audio need legal and consent review before F2 sales, which slows the enterprise path. Its strengths are process and rigour rather than look or identity, and its distinctiveness is about 5. The Tailwind 4 and copy-in migration is still M-effort across every screen.

reviews.yes_case: Clay Coach is a full-app redesign on shadcn/ui (Base UI) with Tailwind v4 tokens, Motion springs, and the react-three-fiber and drei stack the repo already ships. It looks warm and tactile: a clay-paper canvas (#F3EFE8), a clay-orange primary, sage for on-track states, cobalt for scores, 24px cards with two-layer shadows that read as pressable, and dark mode as a first-class token set. 3D appears only on the persona bust and the live caller; data screens stay flat with hairlines, so the debrief and manager views still look serious. The live call is a full-screen console. The clay caller breathes and its jaw follows audio level, its halo turns amber when an objection lands, captions run in speaker lanes, a six-step talk-track rail tracks progress, and five rubric bars stay hatched and provisional until a transcript quote confirms each one. Coach cues are typed (next question, objection alert, watch-out, talk-track step), carry a confidence value and the transcript line that triggered them, and can be set to On, Quiet (tray only) or Off. The library has facets for role, industry, difficulty, objection, mode and source. A New persona tile opens a four-step wizard that takes five source types, drafts persona, scenario and rubric, and tags each field with the sentence it came from; saving exports the same JSON recipe a contributor would submit. A Model Ledger chip shows the model, latency, tokens and estimated cost behind each AI surface. Against today's app, a chat box with no feedback and a three-item dropdown become a coaching console, a browsable catalog and a visible invitation to contribute. It is the most distinctive identity in the set, and it keeps 3D cost to a few surfaces.
reviews.no_case: The persona library is the soft spot. The proposal never commits to a launch count and admits breadth is a content problem, so the UI could ship with a thin catalog. The 2-second cue budget needs a fast parallel coach channel the backend does not have yet. The proposal's own risk section says the playful clay look may read as unserious to enterprise and call-centre buyers. Moving to Tailwind v4 and a new component base on every screen is a large migration for a repo that is on Tailwind 3.4 today, and the parametric busts plus a live R3F canvas add weight on low-end Android and embedded webviews.

reviews.yes_case: Cockpit Dark Command Center is a dark-first, keyboard-first control room on shadcn/ui over Radix, with Cmd-K for every action and a visible keycap beside each command. The palette is near-black (#0A0A0C canvas, #111116 surfaces) with 1px hairlines instead of shadows, one blue accent (#6E8BFF) for actions and focus, and a teal live state. Geist and Geist Mono use tabular figures for timers and scores. A full light token set at parity sits behind a palette toggle. The shell is a 48px icon rail that expands to labels. The library is a dense keyboard-row table with a 240px facet rail that shows counts, saved views, a card-grid toggle and a preview drawer. The progress view has a criterion-by-week heatmap and a Focus this week card, and the manager view reuses the same table and drawer so managers learn one product. The live call is three resizable panes kept sparse on purpose: a transcript in two speaker lanes with inline objection and rubric marks, a talk-track rail with ticks, and a right pane that shows at most one amber whisper cue, an objection alert and eight rubric meters that stay provisional until two turns of evidence exist. Coach latency is shown in the top bar. Coach events are typed and confidence-gated, and the live meters use the same grader as the debrief, so live and final scores agree by construction. The debrief splits a report from a sticky transcript; each number links to its quote, and a provenance chip says whether a model or the keyword fallback graded the call. Against today's app, a chat app and a three-item select become a professional console with a 120-pair catalog of zod-validated persona files that contributors can PR, and a model-chip row that makes OpenAI usage visible. It states its conditions honestly and keeps Tailwind 3 and the existing stack, so the migration risk is the lowest of the top three.
reviews.no_case: It is the least distinctive of the advancing three. Dark, dense, hairline-bordered and Cmd-K-first is now a familiar developer-tool pattern, so reviewers may see a Linear-style clone rather than a product identity; the proposal's own distinctiveness score is 7. Keyboard-first density is a poor fit for casual reps, for managers who want a dashboard, and for phone users, and the mobile tab bar only partly fixes that. Its live-coaching score is conditional: the proposal says the UI alone would score about 5, and the coach stream with its 1.5-second target is not built. The 120-persona target only reaches the 5.0 standard by the proposal's own note, and a launch of about 60 falls below it.

reviews.yes_case: Geist Signal Console is a calm, monochrome product. It uses Geist Sans and Geist Mono at 400, 500 and 600 only, black primary buttons, 1px #EBEBEB hairlines and 8px cards, on shadcn/ui over the existing Tailwind 3 setup, so the phase-one migration stays small. One teal signal (#14B8A6) carries all live AI state as a 1px ring and a rule, never as body text; the blurry orb is replaced by that ring, which pulses only while the coach has a cue. Every AI output carries a provenance chip with its model and latency, and the progress view shows cost per session. The live call is three resizable panes: a call pane with a state pill (caller speaking, your turn, coach thinking), a mono timer and mute; a transcript of hairline-separated turns with inline markers such as Objection: price; and a 320px coach rail with a Next move card that has a Why? line-6 evidence link, Accept and Dismiss, and six rubric meters that tick with a mono delta after each rep turn. Coach budgets are explicit: first cue within 2 seconds at the 50th percentile, meters within 4 seconds, at most one cue per turn, and Silent, Whisper or Guided levels. The library has curated rows (Start here, Objections under pressure, Industry packs), a three-column card grid and a Sheet with a Fork action, and it targets 200 persona-scenario pairs in 20 industry folders. The wizard finds and quotes sources before it drafts anything, then runs a dry run and offers Save or Export as PR. Against today's app, a blurry orb, a three-item select and a flat list become a readable, routed product with a phased rollout that keeps the live demo working, and model claims stay honest until they ship.
reviews.no_case: It is the most likely of the three to read as a Vercel clone. Its own distinctiveness score is 6.5 and this juror rates it lower, because monochrome with black buttons and hairlines is a look many dev-tool sites already use. Cold restraint may land badly with rep-facing and buyer-facing audiences. The proposal leaves Geist's licence unverified, which must be settled before an MIT release. The per-turn gpt-4.1-mini call that makes the 2-second cue budget work roughly doubles per-turn API cost, and the 200-pair library depends on human review that has no named owner.

reviews.yes_case: Game Tape Skill Path wraps every rep in a skill tree, XP, day streaks and opt-in leagues, using a sports game-tape look instead of a mascot. Light app surfaces sit on a dark stage for the live call, the debrief header and the landing hero. Bricolage Grotesque handles titles, Inter handles UI and transcripts, and JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals handles timers, XP and scores. Colour has a job each: rep blue for actions, XP gold only for XP, streak orange only for streaks, mastery green for mastered skills, violet for whispered cues, and rose for End and grade. The progress page is the centrepiece: six branches (Opening, Discovery, Objections, Pricing, Closing, Booking) of five-level skill nodes that fill with a ring sweep, plus a seven-day streak strip, criterion radials and a league ladder. The pre-call briefing shows which node the call sits on and the XP at stake. The live call has a centred orb, a transcript with criterion chips on credited turns, a 320px coach rail with a violet now-cue card, a talk-track path, five live meters with delta flashes, and a streak flame after three rubric hits in a row. The debrief lands a grade ring and reward chips that move a skill node from level 2 to 3, with a moment timeline that jumps to evidence. The library is a card grid with best-score rings, filters and a dashed Build with AI first tile. Against today's app it gives reps a reason to return tomorrow, and it turns personas into a curriculum in which each persona carries objections, difficulty and rubric weights. Its rule that heuristic scores earn no XP is the right integrity call, and the wizard must pass a two-minute dry run before it saves.
reviews.no_case: The look leans toward consumer-app gamification (XP, streaks, leagues, a skill tree) that the proposal itself says call-centre managers and enterprise buyers may find childish, and the sports language is a thin coat over the same mechanics. It adds a second product on top of the core loop, so the call screen competes with badges and XP. Its live coaching cadence is weak: one cue every 20 to 25 seconds, and a self-score of 5.2 that the proposal says holds only if latency stays under 2 seconds. The landing strip says Built on OpenAI Realtime API, while the voice path in this repo is ElevenLabs. A fund reviewer would catch that overclaim.

reviews.yes_case: Spatial Glass Call Window treats every screen as floating glass panes over a dark canvas: 28px-radius windows with a 40px backdrop blur, a 1px specular edge, four depth tiers, and a floating glass dock. It is the most visually current proposal in the set and the most distinctive. The live call is a 960px floating window with a centred 3D orb as its emotional focus, a glass transcript lane below, a talk-track rail on the left, and a coach HUD on the right with dotted rubric meters that settle to solid when the grade lands. Whispered cue chips slide from the window edge and fade after eight seconds. The debrief is a paper-glass light theme for reading and print, with a replay ribbon whose markers scrub the transcript to the exact turn. The progress view is a bento grid with a skill radar and an objection heatmap. The wizard is a centred 760px window with a source detector that recognises the type of pasted text and streams a draft card whose citation chips highlight the source sentence in a split view. Motion is spring-based, with reduced-transparency and reduced-motion fallbacks. Against today's app it makes the product feel like a new category rather than a template. Its two-channel design, with the persona on gpt-realtime over the Realtime API and a separate coach model, is the most explicit Realtime API showcase for OpenAI's fund, and a models ribbon names the cost per call.
reviews.no_case: Coaching is not live in the sense the brief means. The coach reads a rolling transcript window only every 5 to 8 seconds, and whispers are throttled to one per 20 seconds, so the cue the rep needs often arrives after the moment; this is the reason its own coaching score is 5.4 and this juror scores it below baseline. Backdrop blur plus a transmission-material orb on every call screen is a real risk on low-end laptops and Android phones, and the proposal admits the glass hurts transcript contrast. Its SaaS viability score is the lowest in the set at 4.5, because buyers may read glass as a gimmick. Moving the persona voice to gpt-realtime is a large voice-stack migration, and a 300-pack library that Codex review will only partly cover is a content effort on top of it.

reviews.yes_case: Cockpit Dark Command Center is a dark, keyboard-first control room on shadcn/ui over Radix Primitives. Cmd-K drives every screen and action, and each command shows its keycap beside its icon so shortcuts teach themselves. The shell is a 48px icon rail that expands to 220px, with a breadcrumb, a Cmd-K trigger and a live-status pill. Dark is the default, but light is a full token set at parity because reps practise in bright offices. The library is a dense keyboard-row table beside a 240px facet rail, with counts beside each role, industry, difficulty, objection and channel option. A right drawer previews the selected persona with Practice, Duplicate and Edit on GitHub, and a card-grid toggle is available. The AI persona wizard is a full-screen dialog in four steps: Source (one drop zone for a job description, product URL, CRM note, ICP or transcript), Persona (a streaming card where fields cite their source), Scenario and rubric (weight sliders that auto-balance to 100), and a 60-second text test call before Save or Export as PR file. The live call is deliberately sparse: a resizable three-pane layout with a talk-track rail, a transcript in two speaker lanes with inline objection and rubric marks, and a coach stack that shows at most one amber whisper cue, an objection alert, and eight rubric meters that read provisional until two turns of evidence exist. The debrief is a split view with a score hero, a criterion table where clicking a quote scrolls to and highlights the transcript line, and a sticky transcript. The manager view is table-first with a team heatmap, using the same components as the rep view. Against today's three-item dropdown and chat-style call, it is quick to use once learned and gives a rep one cue at a time instead of a wall of advice.
reviews.no_case: It is the most familiar look on the list. A dark, Cmd-K-first shell on shadcn is what many developer and SaaS tools already look like, so it swaps one default template for another, and the proposal itself scores its uniqueness at 7. Its library launches at about 120 pairs, which the proposal says sits exactly on the bar and drops below it at a launch under about 60, so the core content requirement has no margin. The keyboard-first spine is an accelerator for power users, and the visible navigation it adds back to cover everyone else dilutes the signature idea.

reviews.yes_case: Geist Signal Console is a monochrome, developer-tool console built on shadcn/ui over Radix. It uses Geist Sans and Geist Mono throughout, 1px hairline borders, black primary buttons, and one teal signal color (#14B8A6) reserved for live AI state. It looks calm and precise rather than template-generic. The live call is three resizable panes: a Call pane with a state pill (Caller speaking, Your turn, Coach thinking) and a mono timer; a transcript of hairline-separated turns with inline markers such as 'Objection: price'; and a Coach rail whose Next move card has a teal top rule, one cue, a 'Why? line 6' evidence link, and Accept or Dismiss. Coach items carry a 'Coach, private' label so they never read as caller speech. A separate coach lane sends each caller turn to gpt-4.1-mini as one structured call, with a p50 first-cue budget of 2 seconds and at most one cue per turn. Rubric meters stay provisional until the debrief. The library is a 200-pack catalogue with curated rows ('Start here', 'Objections under pressure'), filter chips, and a three-column card grid. Each persona is a zod-validated JSON file that also serves as the OpenAI Structured Outputs schema, so contributor PRs and wizard output are checked the same way. The wizard has five steps (Source, Analyze, Persona, Scenario and rubric, Test and publish). Every generated field either quotes its source or is marked inferred in amber, and the flow ends with a dry run and Save or Export as PR. Against today's three-item select, silent calls and generic blurred orb, this gives reps a clear coaching rail and gives managers a real surface. OpenAI usage is visible through provenance chips showing model and latency on each AI output, and the proposal is honest that voice is ElevenLabs today and that an OpenAI Realtime adapter is planned, not claimed.
reviews.no_case: It looks like Vercel. Geist, black buttons and hairline borders are one company's house style, and the proposal itself warns that monochrome reads cold to sales buyers and invites a clone, which leaves the teal signal as the only original idea. The font license is flagged by the proposal as unverified, so it cannot ship as open source until that is checked. The 200-persona launch is a human-review content job that the design cannot solve, and the proposal gives no plan for it.

reviews.yes_case: Spatial Glass Call Window treats practice as a floating instrument. It uses a dark canvas, layered translucent glass windows with a 1px specular edge, and a 960px call window with a 28px radius centred on the stage. The orb sits at the centre of the call, breathing at idle and moving with mic or persona audio, with the persona name, a temperament chip and a mono timer above it. Glass transcript bubbles run in a scrolling lane below. A left ornament holds the talk-track rail with the current stop glowing. A right ornament holds the coach HUD, with rubric meters that stay dotted until they settle and a next-best-question card. Whispered cues slide in from the window edge as one-line chips and fade after eight seconds. The dock is a floating glass bar, and during a live call it collapses to a single red End control so nothing competes with the orb. The debrief switches to a light paper-glass theme for reading and printing. Its replay ribbon has markers for cues, objections and score jumps that scrub the transcript, and the medallion starts provisional and settles when the grade lands. The persona wizard is a centred 760px window with a source detector that recognises job descriptions, URLs, CRM notes, ICPs and transcripts as they are pasted, and a draft card that fills field by field with citation chips that light the source sentence. Compared with today's blurry gradient orb and chat screen, it is the most distinctive look on the list, makes the call itself the hero, and shows its models in a live ribbon (gpt-realtime for voice, gpt-4.1-mini for grading and cues).
reviews.no_case: Glass over transcripts hurts contrast and reading speed during a live call. A backdrop blur plus a transmission-material WebGL orb is the heaviest thing on screen, on exactly the older laptops and phones reps use to practise. Its coach channel reads the transcript every 5 to 8 seconds, which cannot meet the 2.5-second cue target it sets for itself, so the live-coaching claim is internally inconsistent. Its own F1 score of 4.5 is the lowest here, and the 300-persona launch is a content promise with no review plan.

reviews.yes_case: Game Tape Skill Path wraps sales practice in a skill tree, streaks and XP. It uses a dark game-tape stage for live calls and debriefs and a light app everywhere else. The Path home shows six branches (Opening, Discovery, Objections, Pricing, Closing, Booking) of five-level nodes. Locked nodes are grey, mastered nodes are green with a gold ring, and open contribution nodes carry a plus mark, so the curriculum is visible. The top bar holds a streak flame chip and an XP chip with a level ring. The library is a three-column card grid with a dashed Build with AI tile first, a best-score ring on each persona, and a right sheet with the brief, talk-track preview and rubric weights. The pre-call briefing frames each call as a node ('Pricing transparency, level 2 of 4') with a 'Win these three things' checklist tied to rubric criteria, each showing the last score, and a Start button labelled Earn 40 XP if goal met. The live call has a violet now-cue card with a throttle, an objection alert that names the criterion it threatens, a talk-track path with checkmarks, five rubric meters that flash a +delta after each rep turn, and coaching modes Off, Subtle and Active. The debrief lands the grade and then animates the reward (+48 XP and a node rising from level 2 to 3). Heuristic scores show an Estimate badge and withhold XP, which is a direct fix for today's fallback warning. Compared with today's flat list and four stat tiles, it gives reps a reason to come back tomorrow and a clear next skill to earn. A Model lab panel shows which OpenAI model ran each step, with latency and token cost.
reviews.no_case: This is gamification in a sales-training product sold to managers and call-centre buyers. XP, streaks, leagues and badges add a whole reward economy the brief never asked for, and the proposal itself concedes it may read as childish to enterprise buyers. The live call is the weakest link: cues are capped at one per 20 to 25 seconds, and its own coach score of 5.2 clears the baseline only if cue latency stays under two seconds, which the proposal has not shown.

reviews.yes_case: Strain and Form Console is a Whoop-style performance console built on shadcn/ui over Base UI, with Tailwind v4 and Motion. Every screen is organised around three readings a rep can take in at a glance: Call Strain (0 to 21, how hard a call was), Form (fitness minus fatigue, whether the rep is sharp for a hard persona), and personal records. Light is the default for practice, library, debrief, progress and team. A dark night canvas is used for the live call, the pre-call briefing and the landing hero. The Practice page is a Today view with your Form ring, one recommended persona with its target strain, and your latest PR. The library shows each persona's expected strain as a bar with a number, so the load is known before the rep dials, and each card carries a Form ring showing recent performance. The pre-call briefing forecasts strain ('14 of 21, Hard'), shows the PR to beat, and offers Voice or Text. The live call has a rail of typed whisper cues (Ask, Objection, Pace, Step, Close), one at a time, that fade after six seconds. It also has a talk-ratio bar with a target band, provisional rubric rings drawn dashed until settled, and a coach latency badge. The debrief shows a Final grade ring that replaces the provisional live scores, quote drawers that jump to the transcript line, and an Under the hood tab with model, prompt version, tokens and cost. Voice is switchable between the OpenAI Realtime API and ElevenLabs behind one VoiceProvider interface, which puts OpenAI voice on equal footing. The team view shows a roster with mini rings and load flags for overloaded and undertrained reps, with private PRs on by default. Against today's flat dashboard and scenario dropdown, it gives a rep a reason to return and a clear sense of readiness, and it makes every model call auditable.
reviews.no_case: The metrics are the weak point. Strain and Form are fitness-tracker ideas carried over without a stated formula for how a sales call maps to fitness minus fatigue, and a rep who learns to chase a ring will optimise for the number rather than the skill. The Whoop and Strava patterns were not researched in this run, so the visual language is unsourced. The 240-persona promise is a large content effort, and the proposal's own E score drops to 4 if fewer than 100 ship.

reviews.yes_case: Clay Coach is the most distinctive whole-app redesign in the set. It is a warm clay-paper system, light by default with a first-class dark mode, built around one memorable character: a soft, parametric clay bust of the caller. The 3D is used only where a persona needs identity (the live caller and pre-rendered library thumbnails). Debriefs and dashboards stay flat with hairline rules, so the serious data still reads as serious. The live call is a console, not a chat app. The clay caller sits centre-stage with a jaw that follows audio and a halo that turns sage when the rep is on track and amber when an objection lands. Captions run in speaker lanes. A six-step talk-track tracker sits on the left with a Next best question card, and five rubric bars sit on the right, hatched while provisional and solid once a transcript quote confirms them. Coach cues arrive as typed cards (next best question, objection alert, watch-out, talk-track step), each with a confidence value and the transcript line that triggered it. A Coach switch (On, Quiet, Off) controls how loudly they arrive. The coach runs as a separate model channel that never speaks to the persona, so the caller stays in character. Today the app gives no feedback until the call ends; this gives the rep the next move while still talking. The library is a faceted, searchable catalogue (role, industry, difficulty, objection type, mode, source) where every persona is a versioned JSON recipe. The first tile is a New persona card that opens the wizard with the current filters applied. The four-step wizard drafts persona, scenario and rubric from pasted context, tags each generated field with its source sentence, and ends in a 60-second test call. The debrief becomes a two-column scorecard with a grade medallion, a rubric radar, and timestamped quotes that scrub audio and transcript to the exact second. The OpenAI story is visible: a Model Ledger chip on every AI surface shows model, latency, tokens and cost, and a /contribute page turns the repo into a front door with an add-a-persona recipe that needs no 3D skills, a good-first-issue board and a Codex CLI quickstart. On paper it meets all three basic needs and exceeds the baseline in identity and contributor design.
reviews.no_case: The clay caller is charming, but it is the one element a sales-call console does not need, and it sits where the rep is looking hardest. One WebGL canvas per screen, pre-rendered thumbnails and a static fallback are mandatory, and low-end Android and embedded webviews are the proposal's own performance risk. The coaching promise rests on a two-second cue budget that needs a fast parallel model channel the backend may not hold. If it fails, the fallback is post-turn hints, which pulls D under 5. The Realtime voice provider has to be built, not just labelled, and the proposal says so. Its own scores (D 5.6, E 5.3) put coaching and the library at the bar, not above it. The library size is never stated, and the proposal admits breadth is a content problem it does not solve. Playful clay reads as unserious to call-centre and enterprise buyers, the F2 audience it wants, and it only offers a flat theme as a compensating fix. Moving from Tailwind 3 to v4 while copying in shadcn components will fork styling across contributors unless a token lint rule is enforced from day one, and the proposal does not budget for that process.

reviews.yes_case: Geist Signal Console is the cleanest, most product-like console in the set. Dark is canonical for the live call: near-black canvas, hairline 1px borders instead of shadows, Geist Sans and Geist Mono throughout, black primary buttons, and a light theme designed in parallel. The one accent is a teal signal that lights only when the coach has something to say. It shows as a thin ring that pulses while a cue is live and never colours body text, so the caller and transcript stay calm. The live call is a three-pane resizable layout. The left pane holds the persona name, a state pill (Caller speaking, Your turn, Coach thinking), a mono timer, a mic meter, and End and grade behind a confirm. The centre is a transcript of hairline-separated turns with timestamps and inline markers such as 'Objection: price'. The right 320px rail holds one Next move card with Accept, Dismiss and a Why? evidence link, a six-meter rubric that ticks with mono deltas after each rep turn, and talk-track progress. Coach items carry a 'Coach, private' label, and Silent, Whisper or Guided modes set how much the coach speaks. The coach is a separate lane: one structured call per caller turn returns one cue, rubric deltas, objection flags and an evidence line, with a p50 first-cue target of two seconds and a Not helpful button whose feedback becomes an eval set. The library opens with curated rows (Start here, Objections under pressure, Industry packs). It is a 200-pair catalogue in which each industry pack is a folder contributors can pull-request, with filters for role, industry, difficulty and objection, and a side sheet with temperament sliders, rubric weights, Start practice, Fork and View file on GitHub. The five-step wizard lists what it found, with quote chips, before drafting any field, and each generated field is either quoted or marked amber as inferred. The debrief opens with a score hero and a provenance chip (graded by gpt-4.1-mini with latency, or an amber heuristic fallback), a sticky criteria rail, and Show in transcript jumps. Progress is a bento with a criteria-by-week heatmap and cost per session. Against today's dropdown and chat-style call, it adds a real coach, a forkable library and a legible scorecard, and the phased, route-based rollout protects the live demo. The OpenAI usage is legible on every AI output, and the maintainer loop is named without overclaiming.
reviews.no_case: Monochrome reads cold to a sales audience, and the proposal says so. Beyond the teal ring the look sits one step from a Vercel-style template with Geist swapped in, which caps distinctiveness near 6 and leaves the unique-design claim thin. The Geist license is unverified by the proposer's own note and must be cleared before an open-source release. The flagship live feature is opt-in in practice: default Silent is the honest setting, because a per-turn structured call roughly doubles API cost and the two-second p50 budget depends on provider speed. D only reaches 6.5 if the team pays for that latency. The 200-pair library is a content project in its own right, with no milestone for launch seed counts. At 200 it earns about 6.5, and below roughly 60 it falls under the bar. The five-step wizard adds a Found screen before any draft, which some reps will find slow. Dark-first risks feeling like a gimmick to buyers who print debriefs, although the light theme is designed alongside. The risks list also contains a pasted Mobbin usage notice. It is noise, not a design risk, and should be stripped from the council record.

reviews.yes_case: Cockpit is a dark, keyboard-first control room built on shadcn/ui over Radix, and it treats reps and managers as power users of one product. The shell is a 48px icon rail that expands to labels, with a breadcrumb and a live-status pill up top. A Cmd-K palette runs everything: start a practice call with any persona by name, create a persona from a URL or pasted text, filter the library, mute, end and grade, or toggle the theme. Every command shows its keycap so shortcuts teach themselves, and visible navigation stays on screen, so the palette is an accelerator rather than a requirement. Density is deliberately split. Library, progress and team are dense tables with keyboard row navigation (j, k, Enter, slash to search) and a criteria-by-week heatmap whose cells carry numbers, not just colour. The live call is sparse: a three-pane resizable layout where the coach stack shows at most one amber whisper cue, objection alerts appear inline in the transcript, and rubric meters read provisional until two turns of evidence exist. Debriefs are a 60/40 split with a sticky transcript and a provenance chip reading graded by gpt-4.1-mini, rubric v3, or an amber heuristic fallback, so each number links to a quote. The persona library has a 240px faceted rail with live counts for role, industry, difficulty, objection type and inbound or outbound, plus saved filter views and a grid/table toggle. The wizard is a full-screen dialog with source-cited streaming drafts, weight sliders that auto-balance to 100, a 60-second text test call and an Export as PR file button. The manager view reuses the rep components: a team heatmap, a sortable rep table with trend and weakest-criterion chips, and an assignment drawer that also lives in Cmd-K. The migration is the cheapest in the set. Tailwind 3 and the existing API routes, grading and session storage stay in place until phase two, and a few days of phase zero gets tokens, Geist, and a light and dark theme at parity. Against today's chat-style call and dropdown, it makes the manager surface real and the in-call coaching legible, in a look that is current.
reviews.no_case: A dark command centre is the current default vocabulary for AI productivity tools, and the proposal says its lineage is Linear's. Distinctiveness is its weakest point, and a reviewer may see a well-made clone rather than a product with its own identity. Cmd-K-first excludes casual reps, phone users and anyone who does not know the keymap. The proposal concedes visible navigation must stay, which makes the keyboard story partly decorative for most users. Dark-first clashes with its own note that reps practise in bright offices, so the light theme must hit AA and true parity, not be an afterthought. The live coaching score of 6.0 is conditional. By the proposer's own count the UI alone is about 5, and the sub-1.5-second coach stream is unpriced backend work. The library at about 120 personas sits at the 5.0 standard and falls below it with fewer, and no launch count is committed. Its dense tables and heatmaps are specified for desktop only, and the mobile layout for the library and team views is not described. The mobile live call is one coach card above the composer, which is close to today's layout. XL effort on a nine-screen migration is the proposal's own big-bang risk, and only strict feature-flag discipline avoids it.

reviews.yes_case: Spatial Glass is the most visually ambitious proposal, and the only one that treats the whole call as a floating instrument. The app sits on a near-black canvas with slow mesh light. The live call is a 960px floating window with a 28px radius, and the persona is a glass orb at the centre, rebuilt with a transmission material that displaces with audio level. Paper-glass light mode is used for debriefs and print, so reading surfaces stay calm. The live call puts the talk-track rail on the left with the current stop glowing, a coach HUD on the right with rubric meters that stay dotted until settled, a next-best question card and an amber objection chip, and the transcript as glass bubbles in a lane below. Whispered cues slide in from the window edge as one-line chips and fade after eight seconds. A cue that is acted on docks into the talk-track rail as a completed stop, so coaching reads as part of the call. The debrief has a replay ribbon with markers for coach cues, objections and score jumps. Clicking a marker scrubs the transcript to that turn, and the grade medallion starts dotted and settles solid when the final grade lands. The wizard is a centred floating window with a source detector that recognises job descriptions, URLs, CRM notes or ICPs as you paste, a streaming draft card with citation chips, and a split source view that highlights the exact sentence. The library holds about 300 JSON persona packs with virtualised cards and a cmdk palette, and each card carries an industry-tinted orb. Progress is a bento grid with sparklines, a skill radar and an objection heatmap, and the manager view adds a coaching queue and a rep drawer. The best contributor idea in the set is the Open prompts drawer on every screen, which links to the actual prompt, rubric JSON and schema, so an editor can change a rubric and watch the debrief change. Against today's flat template and chat call, it is the most memorable and the most current in look.
reviews.no_case: Glass over text is a readability and contrast problem. The proposal's own mitigations (80 percent fills on text panes, a reduced-transparency mode and solid fallbacks) concede that transcripts, rubric copy and coach text will read worse than on the flat competitors. Backdrop blur at 40px with a transmission-material orb is GPU-heavy on older laptops and phones. The proposal caps the orb at 30 fps on mobile and falls back to a 2D gradient, so many users will never see the best version. The coaching spec contradicts itself: the coach channel reads a rolling transcript window every five to eight seconds, yet the target is a cue visible within 2.5 seconds of the rep finishing a sentence. Those numbers cannot both hold without a redesign, and the proposer's own D of 5.4 reflects it. The 300-pack library is the largest content commitment in the set, and the proposal lists it as a risk without a launch floor. The voice path depends on switching the persona to gpt-realtime with ElevenLabs behind a flag. That is a backend change rather than a UI change, and the brief requires voice to keep working as it does. F1 is the weakest business case of the five: a glass aesthetic does not create SaaS margin, and the proposer's own 4.5 for a crowded market is right. Glass is also borrowed from visionOS, which may read as imitation in a sales-training tool and can date quickly.

reviews.yes_case: Clearcall is the accessibility-first answer, and it is well built. The canvas is warm paper (#F7F7F4) with ink at 17.4:1. Violet is reserved for AI coach cues only. Every control has 3:1 edges and a 44px minimum target, with 56px live-call controls. No state is conveyed by colour alone, motion is off under reduced-motion, and the breathing orb becomes a plain status word (Listening, Speaking, Thinking). The live call has three named landmark regions (Transcript, Coach, Controls) behind a skip link. Coaching arrives as text with a type label and a Dismiss button. Talk-track steps read Done, Next or Missed with icon and word. Criterion rows show points, a bar and a status word, tagged Provisional until the grader confirms each turn. Its screen-reader policy is the sharpest rule set in the set: one polite announcement per cue, queued, no more than one every eight seconds, and score announcements only when a criterion crosses a band, once per call. The library has four facets (Role, Industry, Difficulty, Objection type) as a filter rail and removable chips, 120-plus personas grouped under pack headers such as 'SDR cold calls (18)', and cards with a 30-second voice preview and twin Create with AI and New manually buttons. The wizard runs source, extract (each field cites its source sentence and is editable), persona dials, rubric weights validated at 100, and a two-minute test call, and its output is a persona file ready for a PR. The debrief shows a model receipt per criterion, with print and JSON export. Compared with today's generic, sometimes low-contrast app, it gives clear, rule-based coaching and a debrief that works for every reader. It also has a procurement angle, since enterprise buyers ask for accessibility compliance, and a CI-enforced axe-core wcag2aaa gate is a checkable signal for OpenAI reviewers and contributors alike.
reviews.no_case: Blunt: this is the least modern proposal here. Warm paper, violet and a conservative type scale read as a calm, well-behaved enterprise form rather than cutting-edge AI tech, and its own A of 7 is the most honest number in its scoring. AAA exceeds what most buyers ask for (AA is the usual procurement line), and 7:1 text, 44px targets and a flat system constrain brand character and crowd the mobile layout, as the proposal admits. Its live-coaching spec has no latency budget and no cost commitment for coach or cue calls. It says cue cadence is a guess until blind and low-vision users test it, and it keeps cues opt-in. D sits at 6.0 on the strength of rules rather than a proven coaching pipeline. The 120-plus persona claim is a content commitment the proposal does not staff, so E is 5.5 at best. The React Aria listing as MIT looks wrong (as far as I know react-aria is Apache-2.0), a small error that matters in a document meant for grant reviewers. Two of its Firecrawl searches errored, which it discloses, so its library and fund facts come from memory rather than research.
